13.2.32.a.m: He modifies the consumption mantra to: 'of the Virāj meter.'

13.2.33.a.s: dakṣiṇasyāṃ vediśroṇyāṃ vājasṛto vimāthīkṛtya surāgrahān bhakṣayanti //
13.2.33.a.d: दक्षिणस्यां वेदिश्रोण्यां वाजसृतो विमाथीकृत्य सुराग्रहान् भक्षयन्ति ॥
13.2.33.a.m: On the southern hip of the vedi, the chariot-runners, having snatched them mutually, consume the surā cups.

13.2.34.a.s: anuyājaiḥ pracarati te vyūḍhāsu srukṣu sārasvataprabhṛtīnām uttareṣāṃ daivatena pracarati //
13.2.34.a.d: अनुयाजैः प्रचरति ते व्यूढासु स्रुक्षु सारस्वतप्रभृतीनाम् उत्तरेषां दैवतेन प्रचरति ॥
13.2.34.a.m: He proceeds with the after-offerings; when they are finished and the offering ladles are set apart, he proceeds with the deity offerings of the later [victims] beginning with the one for Sarasvatī.

13.2.35.a.s: api vā yatraivetareṣāṃ paśūnāṃ vapābhiḥ pracaret //
13.2.35.a.d: अपि वा यत्रैवेतरेषां पशूनां वपाभिः प्रचरेत् ॥
13.2.35.a.m: Or rather, [he proceeds with them] wherever he would proceed with the omenta of the other animals.

13.2.36.a.s: yatro haiva havirbhis tad dhavirbhir mārutyā avadānīyān ṛtvigbhya upaharati //
13.2.36.a.d: यत्रो हैव हविर्भिस् तद् धविर्भिर् मारुत्या अवदानीयान् ऋत्विग्भ्य उपहरति ॥
13.2.36.a.m: And wherever [he proceeds] with the oblations, there he presents the portions to be cut of the [victim] for the Maruts to the priests.

13.2.37.a.s: anavadānīyān vājasṛdbhyas tāni dakṣiṇasyāṃ vediśroṇyāṃ vājasṛto vimāthīkṛtya bhakṣayanti //
13.2.37.a.d: अनवदानीयान् वाजसृद्भ्यस् तानि दक्षिणस्यां वेदिश्रोण्यां वाजसृतो विमाथीकृत्य भक्षयन्ति ॥
13.2.37.a.m: The portions not to be cut he presents to the chariot-runners; those the chariot-runners, having snatched them mutually, consume on the southern hip of the vedi.

13.2.38.a.s: kakudo rājaputro dhruvagopo naivāragopo vā prāśnāti / ubhau vā / sarvaṃ vā kakudam //
13.2.38.a.d: ककुदो राजपुत्रो ध्रुवगोपो नैवारगोपो वा प्राश्नाति । उभौ वा । सर्वं वा ककुदम् ॥
13.2.38.a.m: The king's son, either the defender of the firm [land] or the defender of wild rice, eats of the hump; or both [eat of it]; or [he eats] the entire hump.

13.2.40.a.m: Having sacrificed with the Vājapeya, he should sacrifice with the Sautrāmaṇī.

13.2.41.a.m: He does not rise to greet anyone.

13.2.42.a.m: It is known [from the Brāhmaṇa]: 'He becomes one with a white umbrella.'

13.3.1.a.m: A king desiring heaven should sacrifice with the Rājasūya.

13.3.2.a.s: taiṣyāḥ paurṇamāsyāḥ purastāt pañcarātre māsi dīkṣeta //
13.3.2.a.d: तैष्याः पौर्णमास्याः पुरस्तात् पञ्चरात्रे मासि दीक्षेत ॥
13.3.2.a.m: He should undergo initiation in the month five days before the full-moon day of the month of Taiṣa.

13.3.3.a.s: yathāsyāṃ parasmin saṃvatsare taiṣyāṃ paurṇamāsyām abhiṣecanīyāyokthyāya dīkṣā pravatsyatīti
13.3.3.a.d: यथास्यां परस्मिन् संवत्सरे तैष्यां पौर्णमास्याम् अभिषेचनीयायोक्थ्याय दीक्षा प्रवत्स्यतीति
13.3.3.a.m: So that, on this same full-moon day of Taiṣa in the following year, the initiation for the Abhiṣecanīya ukthya sacrifice will take place.

13.3.4.a.m: He should first sacrifice with the Jyotiṣṭoma Agniṣṭoma.

13.3.6.a.s: śatasahasraṃ sarveṣu rājasūyikeṣu someṣu samaśaḥ prativibhajyānvahaṃ dadāti //
13.3.6.a.d: शतसहस्रं सर्वेषु राजसूयिकेषु सोमेषु समशः प्रतिविभज्यान्वहं ददाति ॥
13.3.6.a.m: Dividing one hundred thousand equally among all the soma sacrifices of the Rājasūya, he gives [it] day by day.

13.3.8.a.m: So that his days have their own proper times; he should assign the remainder.

13.3.9.a.m: Because of the day-by-day injunction of the iṣṭis and animal sacrifices of the Rājasūya.

13.3.10.a.m: From the distinctness of their sacrificial gifts, one should understand the distinctness of the iṣṭis.

13.3.11.a.s: anyaddiśām aveṣṭeḥ pṛthakdakṣiṇāni tāny ekatantrāṇi bhavanti //
13.3.11.a.d: अन्यद्दिशाम् अवेष्टेः पृथक्दक्षिणानि तान्य् एकतन्त्राणि भवन्ति ॥
13.3.11.a.m: Except for the Aveṣṭi of the quarters; those have separate sacrificial gifts but share a single sacrificial framework.

13.3.12.a.m: On the next day, he should sacrifice day by day with [the offerings] beginning with the Ānumata.

13.3.13.a.s: anumatyai puroḍāśam aṣṭākapālaṃ nirvapatīti yathāsamāmnātam / pim̐ṣann ānumataṃ paścād uttarataś ca vyavaśātayati //
13.3.13.a.d: अनुमत्यै पुरोडाशम् अष्टाकपालं निर्वपतीति यथासमाम्नातम् । पिम्̐षन्न् आनुमतं पश्चाद् उत्तरतश् च व्यवशातयति ॥
13.3.13.a.m: As traditionally taught: 'He offers a sacrificial cake on eight potsherds to Anumati'; while grinding [the grains for] the Ānumata, he casts [some] aside to the west and to the north.

13.3.14.a.s: ye pratyañcaḥ śamyāyā avaśīyante taṃ nairṛtam ekakapālaṃ kuryāt //
13.3.14.a.d: ये प्रत्यञ्चः शम्याया अवशीयन्ते तं नैरृतम् एककपालं कुर्यात् ॥
13.3.14.a.m: Those which fall toward the west of the yoke-pin, he should make that [into] a Nairṛta [cake] on one potsherd.

13.3.15.a.m: Having put down the potsherds for the Ānumata, he puts down the potsherd for the Nairṛta.

13.3.16.a.m: Having placed [the cake for] the Ānumata [near the fire], he proceeds with the Nairṛta.

13.3.17.a.s: vīhi svāhāhutiṃ juṣāṇas \\ iti sruveṇa gārhapatye juhoti //
13.3.17.a.d: वीहि स्वाहाहुतिं जुषाणस् \\ इति स्रुवेण गार्हपत्ये जुहोति ॥
13.3.17.a.m: With the sruva spoon he offers in the gārhapatya fire with: 'Enjoying the offering, savor [it], svāhā!'

13.3.18.a.m: He makes a single firebrand from the dakṣiṇāgni fire smoke.

13.3.19.a.s: parācīnaṃ dakṣiṇāparam avāntaradeśam̐ hṛtvā svakṛta iriṇe pradare vopasamādhāya juṣāṇā nirṛtir vetu svāhā \\ iti // visraṃsikāyāḥ kāṇḍābhyām̐ sarvahutaṃ nairṛtaṃ juhoti //
13.3.19.a.d: पराचीनं दक्षिणापरम् अवान्तरदेशम्̐ हृत्वा स्वकृत इरिणे प्रदरे वोपसमाधाय जुषाणा निरृतिर् वेतु स्वाहा \\ इति ॥ विस्रंसिकायाः काण्डाभ्याम्̐ सर्वहुतं नैरृतं जुहोति ॥
13.3.19.a.m: Carrying it away turned away toward the intermediate southwest quarter, and having added fuel to it in a natural cleft or chasm, with: 'May Nirṛti, enjoying [it], savor [it], svāhā!' he offers the Nairṛta wholly offered with two pieces of a splitting reed;

13.3.20.a.s: aṅguṣṭhābhyām eṣa te nirṛte bhāgas \\ iti vā //
13.3.20.a.d: अङ्गुष्ठाभ्याम् एष ते निरृते भागस् \\ इति वा ॥
13.3.20.a.m: or with the two thumbs, with: 'This is your share, O Nirṛti!'

13.3.21.a.d: वासो ऽभिन्नान्तं दक्षिणा कृष्णं वासः कृष्णदशम् ॥
13.3.21.a.m: The sacrificial gift is an uncut garment, a black garment with black fringes.

13.3.22.a.m: Having poured water around, they return without looking back.

13.3.23.a.s: svāhā namo ya idaṃ cakāra \\ iti punar etya gārhapatye juhoti //
13.3.23.a.d: स्वाहा नमो य इदं चकार \\ इति पुनर् एत्य गार्हपत्ये जुहोति ॥
13.3.23.a.m: Having returned, he offers in the gārhapatya fire with: 'Svāhā, homage to him who has done this!'

13.3.24.a.s: anumatena pracarati ya udañco 'vaśīyante tān udak paretya śuktyā valmīkavapām uddhatya \\ idam aham amuṣyāmuṣyāyaṇasya kṣetriyam avayaje \\ iti śuktyā valmīkavapāyāṃ juhoti / tām apidadhāti \\ idama ham amuṣyāmuṣyāyaṇasya kṣetriyam apidadhe \\ iti śuktyā valmīkavapayā vā //
13.3.24.a.d: अनुमतेन प्रचरति य उदञ्चो ऽवशीयन्ते तान् उदक् परेत्य शुक्त्या वल्मीकवपाम् उद्धत्य \\ इदम् अहम् अमुष्यामुष्यायणस्य क्षेत्रियम् अवयजे \\ इति शुक्त्या वल्मीकवपायां जुहोति । ताम् अपिदधाति \\ इदम हम् अमुष्यामुष्यायणस्य क्षेत्रियम् अपिदधे \\ इति शुक्त्या वल्मीकवपया वा ॥
13.3.24.a.m: He proceeds with the Ānumata; those [grains] which fall toward the north, going northward with them and digging out an anthill's embryo with a pearl-shell, he offers with the pearl-shell into the anthill's embryo with: 'Here do I sacrifice away the inherited disease of this person, son of that person!' He covers it with the pearl-shell or with the anthill's embryo with: 'Here do I cover up the inherited disease of this person, son of that person!'

13.3.25.a.s: ādityaṃ caruṃ nirvapatīti tad uttarāsv āsām uttamā //
13.3.25.a.d: आदित्यं चरुं निर्वपतीति तद् उत्तरास्व् आसाम् उत्तमा ॥
13.3.25.a.m: As for 'he offers a pap to the Ādityas', that is the last among the subsequent ones of these.

13.3.26.a.s: āgrayaṇeṣṭis tayeṣṭvā śvo bhūte sarasvatyai caruṃ nirvapati / sarasvate caruṃ mithunau gāvau dakṣiṇā //
13.3.26.a.d: आग्रयणेष्टिस् तयेष्ट्वा श्वो भूते सरस्वत्यै चरुं निर्वपति । सरस्वते चरुं मिथुनौ गावौ दक्षिणा ॥
13.3.26.a.m: The first-fruits sacrifice (Āgrayaṇeṣṭi); having sacrificed with it, on the next day he offers a pap to Sarasvatī, a pap to Sarasvat; a mating pair of cattle is the sacrificial gift.

13.3.27.a.s: śvo bhūte cāturmāsyāny ālabhate / taiḥ saṃvatsaraṃ yajate //
13.3.27.a.d: श्वो भूते चातुर्मास्यान्य् आलभते । तैः संवत्सरं यजते ॥
13.3.27.a.m: On the next day, he undertakes the Cāturmāsya sacrifices; he sacrifices with them for a year.

13.3.28.a.m: He does not combine the Śunāsīrīya together [with the others].

13.3.29.a.m: On the next day, he sacrifices day by day with [the offerings] beginning with the Indraturīya.

13.3.30.a.s: āgneyam aṣṭākapālaṃ nirvapatīti yathāsamāmnātam / caturhavir indraturīyam / tat saṃgrāme nirvapet //
13.3.30.a.d: आग्नेयम् अष्टाकपालं निर्वपतीति यथासमाम्नातम् । चतुर्हविर् इन्द्रतुरीयम् । तत् संग्रामे निर्वपेत् ॥
13.3.30.a.m: As traditionally taught: 'He offers [a cake] on eight potsherds to Agni'; the Indraturīya has four oblations; he should offer that in battle.

13.3.31.a.s: etasyā eva rātrer niśāyāṃ pañcedhmīyena yajeta //
13.3.31.a.d: एतस्या एव रात्रेर् निशायां पञ्चेध्मीयेन यजेत ॥
13.3.31.a.m: At night of this very night, he should sacrifice with the Pañcedhmīya.

13.3.32.a.m: At night they proceed with the Apāmārga offering.

13.3.33.a.s: sāyam̐ hute 'gnihotre 'pāṃ nyayanād apāmārgān āhṛtya tān saktūn kṛtvā dakṣiṇāgner ekolmukaṃ dhūpayati //
13.3.33.a.d: सायम्̐ हुते ऽग्निहोत्रे ऽपां न्ययनाद् अपामार्गान् आहृत्य तान् सक्तून् कृत्वा दक्षिणाग्नेर् एकोल्मुकं धूपयति ॥
13.3.33.a.m: When the evening Agnihotra has been offered, having brought apāmārga plants from a pool of water and made them into groats, he makes a single firebrand from the dakṣiṇāgni fire smoke.

13.3.34.a.s: parācīnam uttarāparam avāntaradeśam̐ hṛtvā svakṛta iriṇe pradare vopasamādhāya // devasya tvā savituḥ prasave 'śvinor bāhubhyāṃ pūṣṇo hastābhyām̐ rakṣaso vadhaṃ juhomi svāhā \\ iti parṇamayenārkamayeṇa vā sruveṇāpāmārgasaktūñ juhoti / indrasya tvaujase juhomi svāhā \\ iti vā / hatam̐ rakṣas \\ iti sruvam anuprahṛtya \\ avadhiṣma rakṣas \\ iti hutvopatiṣṭhate //
13.3.34.a.d: पराचीनम् उत्तरापरम् अवान्तरदेशम्̐ हृत्वा स्वकृत इरिणे प्रदरे वोपसमाधाय ॥ देवस्य त्वा सवितुः प्रसवे ऽश्विनोर् बाहुभ्यां पूष्णो हस्ताभ्याम्̐ रक्षसो वधं जुहोमि स्वाहा \\ इति पर्णमयेनार्कमयेण वा स्रुवेणापामार्गसक्तूञ् जुहोति । इन्द्रस्य त्वौजसे जुहोमि स्वाहा \\ इति वा । हतम्̐ रक्षस् \\ इति स्रुवम् अनुप्रहृत्य \\ अवधिष्म रक्षस् \\ इति हुत्वोपतिष्ठते ॥
13.3.34.a.m: Carrying it away turned away toward the intermediate northwest quarter, and having added fuel to it in a natural cleft or chasm, with a sruva spoon made of palāśa wood or made of arka wood he offers the apāmārga groats with: 'At the impulse of divine Savitṛ, with the arms of the Aśvins, with the hands of Pūṣan, I offer the slaying of the demon, svāhā!' or with: 'For Indra's strength I offer you, svāhā!' Having cast the sruva spoon after [the offering] with: 'The demon is slain!', having offered, he reveres [the fire] with: 'We have slain the demon!'

13.3.35.a.s: varo dakṣiṇā yad vaste tad dakṣiṇā //
13.3.35.a.d: वरो दक्षिणा यद् वस्ते तद् दक्षिणा ॥
13.3.35.a.m: A boon is the sacrificial gift; what he wears is the sacrificial gift.

13.3.36.a.s: etenaiva yajeta yaḥ pāpmano bibhīyāt pañcedhmīyena carati / caturdhāhavanīyaṃ pratidiśaṃ vyūhati / madhye pañcamam / pṛthag idhmān upasamādhāya ye devāḥ puraḥsadas \\ iti pradakṣiṇam anuparikrāman pratidiśaṃ catasra āhutīr juhoti / madhye pañcamīm / samūḍham̐ rakṣas \\ iti madhya idhmān abhisamuhya \\ agnaye rakṣoghne svāhā \\ iti pañcagṛhītena pañcottarā rathaḥ pañcavāhī dakṣiṇā / praṣṭivāhī vā //
13.3.36.a.d: एतेनैव यजेत यः पाप्मनो बिभीयात् पञ्चेध्मीयेन चरति । चतुर्धाहवनीयं प्रतिदिशं व्यूहति । मध्ये पञ्चमम् । पृथग् इध्मान् उपसमाधाय ये देवाः पुरःसदस् \\ इति प्रदक्षिणम् अनुपरिक्रामन् प्रतिदिशं चतस्र आहुतीर् जुहोति । मध्ये पञ्चमीम् । समूढम्̐ रक्षस् \\ इति मध्य इध्मान् अभिसमुह्य \\ अग्नये रक्षोघ्ने स्वाहा \\ इति पञ्चगृहीतेन पञ्चोत्तरा रथः पञ्चवाही दक्षिणा । प्रष्टिवाही वा ॥
13.3.36.a.m: He who fears evil should sacrifice with this very [rite]. He proceeds with the Pañcedhmīya: he spreads out the āhavanīya fire in four directions toward each quarter, the fifth in the middle; having placed separate firewood bundles on them, circumambulating sunwise, he offers four oblations toward each quarter with: 'The gods who sit in front...', the fifth in the middle; having swept the firewood bundles together into the middle with: 'The demon is swept together!', with five ladlefuls [he offers] the five subsequent ones with: 'To Agni the demon-slayer, svāhā!' A chariot drawn by five [horses] is the sacrificial gift, or one drawn by a side-horse.

13.3.37.a.s: tenaiva yajeta yo rakṣobhyo bibhīyāt piśācebhyo vā / taṃ ca yat kāmayate tad dadyāt //
13.3.37.a.d: तेनैव यजेत यो रक्षोभ्यो बिभीयात् पिशाचेभ्यो वा । तं च यत् कामयते तद् दद्यात् ॥
13.3.37.a.m: He who fears demons or Piśācas should sacrifice with that very [rite]; and he should give him whatever he desires.

13.3.38.a.m: On the next day, he should sacrifice with the single-oblation [offerings] to the gods.

13.3.39.a.s: dhātre puroḍāśaṃ dvādaśakapālaṃ nirvapatīti yathāsamāmnātam / mithunau gāvau dakṣiṇā vatsatarī vā //
13.3.39.a.d: धात्रे पुरोडाशं द्वादशकपालं निर्वपतीति यथासमाम्नातम् । मिथुनौ गावौ दक्षिणा वत्सतरी वा ॥
13.3.39.a.m: As traditionally taught: 'He offers a sacrificial cake on twelve potsherds to Dhātṛ'; a mating pair of cattle is the sacrificial gift, or a heifer.

13.3.40.a.m: 'A cow that has been mated, or one being mated', according to some.

13.3.41.a.m: One who desires offspring or who desires cattle should sacrifice with them.

13.3.42.a.s: āmayāvinaṃ yājayed vā dhātāraṃ madhyataḥ kṛtvā prajākāmaḥ putrair dhātāram uttamaṃ kṛtvāmayāvī paśunā yajate //
13.3.42.a.d: आमयाविनं याजयेद् वा धातारं मध्यतः कृत्वा प्रजाकामः पुत्रैर् धातारम् उत्तमं कृत्वामयावी पशुना यजते ॥
13.3.42.a.m: Or he should cause a sick person to sacrifice: one who desires offspring, having placed Dhātṛ in the middle, sacrifices with sons; a sick person, having made Dhātṛ the last, sacrifices with an animal.

13.3.43.a.m: On the next day, he sacrifices day by day with the Triṣaṃyuktas.

13.3.44.a.s: āgnāvaiṣṇavam ekādaśakapālaṃ nirvapatīti yathāsamāmnātaṃ prathamaṃ triṣaṃyuktaṃ tena yajñakāmo yajeta / agnīṣomīyam ekādaśakapālaṃ nirvapatīti yathāsamāmnātaṃ madhyamaṃ triṣaṃyuktaṃ vīrajanam̐ samāmananti / somāpauṣṇaṃ caruṃ nirvapatīti yathāsamāmnātam uttamaṃ triṣaṃyuktaṃ tena paśukāmo yajeta / vaiśvānaraṃ dvādaśakapālaṃ nirvapatīti tena grāmakāmo yajeta / vāruṇaṃ yavamayaṃ carum iti sarvataḥ prādeśamātro vāruṇaś carur bhavati / yogyo 'śvo vyuptavaho vā dakṣiṇā / samānatantrau vaiśvānaravāruṇāv eke samāmananti //
13.3.44.a.d: आग्नावैष्णवम् एकादशकपालं निर्वपतीति यथासमाम्नातं प्रथमं त्रिषंयुक्तं तेन यज्ञकामो यजेत । अग्नीषोमीयम् एकादशकपालं निर्वपतीति यथासमाम्नातं मध्यमं त्रिषंयुक्तं वीरजनम्̐ समामनन्ति । सोमापौष्णं चरुं निर्वपतीति यथासमाम्नातम् उत्तमं त्रिषंयुक्तं तेन पशुकामो यजेत । वैश्वानरं द्वादशकपालं निर्वपतीति तेन ग्रामकामो यजेत । वारुणं यवमयं चरुम् इति सर्वतः प्रादेशमात्रो वारुणश् चरुर् भवति । योग्यो ऽश्वो व्युप्तवहो वा दक्षिणा । समानतन्त्रौ वैश्वानरवारुणाव् एके समामनन्ति ॥
13.3.44.a.m: With the rule: 'He pours out an offering to Agni and Viṣṇu on eleven potsherds', [this is] the first triad, as handed down; one who desires a sacrifice should sacrifice with it. With the rule: 'He pours out an offering to Agni and Soma on eleven potsherds', [this is] the middle triad, as handed down; they recite it as generating heroes. With the rule: 'He pours out a mess of boiled rice to Soma and Pūṣan', [this is] the last triad, as handed down; one who desires cattle should sacrifice with it. With the rule: 'He pours out an offering to Vaiśvānara on twelve potsherds', one who desires a village should sacrifice with it. With the rule: 'A barley mess of boiled rice to Varuṇa', the mess of boiled rice to Varuṇa is a span in size in all directions. A trained horse or a draught ox is the sacrificial gift. Some recite that the offerings to Vaiśvānara and to Varuṇa have the same sacrificial framework.

13.4.1.a.m: On the following day, [there are] the thirteen sacrificial oblations of the jewel-holders.

13.4.2.a.m: He pours out [the oblations] daily in the houses of the intimates of the sacrificer.

13.4.3.a.s: yasyayasya gṛhe nirvapati tasyatasya gṛhād iṣṭipariveṣaṇaṃ dakṣiṇā ca //
13.4.3.a.d: यस्ययस्य गृहे निर्वपति तस्यतस्य गृहाद् इष्टिपरिवेषणं दक्षिणा च ॥
13.4.3.a.m: In whichever house he pours out [the oblation], from that very house comes the distribution of the sacrifice and the sacrificial gift.

13.4.4.a.s: bārhaspatyaṃ caruṃ nirvapati brahmaṇo gṛhe / śitipṛṣṭho dakṣiṇeti yathāsamāmnātam / purohitasyaikeṣām //
13.4.4.a.d: बार्हस्पत्यं चरुं निर्वपति ब्रह्मणो गृहे । शितिपृष्ठो दक्षिणेति यथासमाम्नातम् । पुरोहितस्यैकेषाम् ॥
13.4.4.a.m: He pours out a mess of boiled rice to Bṛhaspati in the house of the brahman priest. 'A white-backed [bull] is the sacrificial gift', as handed down. According to some, [it is performed in the house] of the royal domestic priest.

13.4.5.a.s: bhagāya caruṃ vā vātāyai gṛhe vicittagarbhā paṣṭhauhī dakṣiṇā //
13.4.5.a.d: भगाय चरुं वा वातायै गृहे विचित्तगर्भा पष्ठौही दक्षिणा ॥
13.4.5.a.m: Or a mess of boiled rice to Bhaga, in the house of the discarded queen; a four-year-old cow whose pregnancy has aborted is the sacrificial gift.

13.4.6.a.s: nairṛtaṃ carum iti sarvato 'ṅguṣṭhamātro nairṛtaś carur bhavati //
13.4.6.a.d: नैरृतं चरुम् इति सर्वतो ऽङ्गुष्ठमात्रो नैरृतश् चरुर् भवति ॥
13.4.6.a.m: With the rule: 'A mess of boiled rice to Nirṛti', the mess of boiled rice to Nirṛti is the size of a thumb in all directions.

13.4.7.a.m: Or, being the size of a thumb-joint, he offers the mess of boiled rice to Nirṛti as an entirely offered [oblation].

13.4.8.a.s: takṣarathakārāv ekasmin gṛhe samavanīyāgneyam aṣṭākapālaṃ nirvapati sarvāyasāni dakṣiṇā govikartrakṣāvāpāv ekasmin gṛhe samavanīya vaiṣṇavaṃ trikapālam iti vatsaḥ śvetaśabalo dakṣiṇā / vaiṣṇavaṃ trikapālaṃ trayodaśaṃ takṣarathakārayor gṛhe / sarvāyasāni dakṣiṇā / takṣṇo rathakārasya vety eke //
13.4.8.a.d: तक्षरथकाराव् एकस्मिन् गृहे समवनीयाग्नेयम् अष्टाकपालं निर्वपति सर्वायसानि दक्षिणा गोविकर्त्रक्षावापाव् एकस्मिन् गृहे समवनीय वैष्णवं त्रिकपालम् इति वत्सः श्वेतशबलो दक्षिणा । वैष्णवं त्रिकपालं त्रयोदशं तक्षरथकारयोर् गृहे । सर्वायसानि दक्षिणा । तक्ष्णो रथकारस्य वेत्य् एके ॥
13.4.8.a.m: Bringing together the carpenter and the chariot-maker into one house, he pours out [an offering] to Agni on eight potsherds; all kinds of iron [tools] are the sacrificial gift. Bringing together the butcher and the dice-caster into one house, with the rule: '[An offering] to Viṣṇu on three potsherds', a white-spotted calf is the sacrificial gift. The thirteenth [oblation] to Viṣṇu on three potsherds is [offered] in the house of the carpenter and chariot-maker; all kinds of iron [tools] are the sacrificial gift. Or, according to some, [in the house] of the carpenter or of the chariot-maker.

13.4.9.a.s: senānyo gṛhe samavanīyāgneyam aṣṭākapālaṃ nirvapatīti hiraṇyaṃ dakṣiṇā //
13.4.9.a.d: सेनान्यो गृहे समवनीयाग्नेयम् अष्टाकपालं निर्वपतीति हिरण्यं दक्षिणा ॥
13.4.9.a.m: Bringing together [the requisites] in the house of the army-commander, with the rule: 'He pours out [an offering] to Agni on eight potsherds', gold is the sacrificial gift.

13.4.10.a.s: raudraṃ gāvīdhukaṃ carum akṣāvāpasya gṛhe śabala udvāro dakṣiṇā / asir vālāvṛtaḥ kesarapāśā vā govyucchanī rajjuḥ //
13.4.10.a.d: रौद्रं गावीधुकं चरुम् अक्षावापस्य गृहे शबल उद्वारो दक्षिणा । असिर् वालावृतः केसरपाशा वा गोव्युच्छनी रज्जुः ॥
13.4.10.a.m: A mess of boiled gavidhuka-grain to Rudra in the house of the dice-caster; a spotted castrated bull is the sacrificial gift, [or] a sword covered with hair, or hair-nooses, or a rope used for cow-driving.

13.4.11.a.s: adhvane svāhā \\ iti pālākalasya gṛhe juhoti //
13.4.11.a.d: अध्वने स्वाहा \\ इति पालाकलस्य गृहे जुहोति ॥
13.4.11.a.m: He offers in the house of the messenger with: 'To the path, svāhā!'

13.4.12.a.m: They call [him] a messenger of untruth. A cane-wound bow is the sacrificial gift.

13.4.13.a.m: Three leather quivers containing arrows are the sacrificial gift.

13.4.14.a.s: aindram uttamaṃ yajamānasya gṛhe nirvapati / anvaham eke bruvate / indrāya sutrāmṇe puroḍāśam ekādaśakapālaṃ ( prati ) nirvapati / indrāyām̐homuce / \ ayaṃ no rājā vṛtrahā \ rājā bhūtvā vṛtraṃ vadhyāt \\ iti sūktavākasyāśīḥṣu hotānuvartayati //
13.4.14.a.d: ऐन्द्रम् उत्तमं यजमानस्य गृहे निर्वपति । अन्वहम् एके ब्रुवते । इन्द्राय सुत्राम्णे पुरोडाशम् एकादशकपालं ( प्रति ) निर्वपति । इन्द्रायाम्̐होमुचे । \ अयं नो राजा वृत्रहा \ राजा भूत्वा वृत्रं वध्यात् \\ इति सूक्तवाकस्याशीःषु होतानुवर्तयति ॥
13.4.14.a.m: He pours out the last [oblation] to Indra in the house of the sacrificer. Some say [he performs them] daily. He pours out a sacrificial cake on eleven potsherds to Indra Sutrāman [and] to Indra Aṃhomuc. In the benedictions of the Sūktavāka, the hotṛ adds: 'May this king of ours, slayer of Vṛtra, having become king, slay Vṛtra!'

13.4.15.a.s: svayamavapannāyā aśvatthaśākhāyai maitraṃ pātraṃ catuḥsrakti karoti //
13.4.15.a.d: स्वयमवपन्नाया अश्वत्थशाखायै मैत्रं पात्रं चतुःस्रक्ति करोति ॥
13.4.15.a.m: Out of a branch of an aśvattha tree that has fallen of itself, he makes a four-cornered vessel for Mitra.

13.4.16.a.s: śvetāṃ śvetavatsām āmrasya dṛtau duhanti / tat svayaṃmūrtam̐ saṃyogena parivahati //
13.4.16.a.d: श्वेतां श्वेतवत्साम् आम्रस्य दृतौ दुहन्ति । तत् स्वयंमूर्तम्̐ संयोगेन परिवहति ॥
13.4.16.a.m: They milk a white cow having a white calf into a skin bag of an āamra tree; that [milk], coagulating of itself, by combination turns into whey.

13.4.17.a.m: Chirned of itself, it separates in the heat of the sun.

13.4.18.a.m: That clarified butter becomes clarified of itself.

13.4.19.a.m: On the Full Moon day of the month of Pauṣa, they initiate the consecrations for the consecratory Ukthya sacrifice.

13.4.20.a.m: The consecratory rite belongs to Mitra and Bṛhaspati.

13.4.21.a.s: pātrasam̐sādanakāle yathārthaṃ pātrāṇi prayunakti sthālīṃ kapālānām̐ sthāne prayunakti //
13.4.21.a.d: पात्रसम्̐सादनकाले यथार्थं पात्राणि प्रयुनक्ति स्थालीं कपालानाम्̐ स्थाने प्रयुनक्ति ॥
13.4.21.a.m: At the time of placing the vessels, he sets out the vessels as needed; he sets out a cooking pot in place of the potsherds.

13.4.22.a.s: maitraṃ caruṃ nirvapaṇakāle bṛhaspataye nirupya mitrāya nirvapatīti / yathā vā triṣphalīkṛteṣu vibhāgamantreṇa karṇām̐ś cākarṇām̐śca taṇḍulān vivicanti / kṣodiṣṭhām̐ś ca sthaviṣṭhām̐ś cety ekeṣām //
13.4.22.a.d: मैत्रं चरुं निर्वपणकाले बृहस्पतये निरुप्य मित्राय निर्वपतीति । यथा वा त्रिष्फलीकृतेषु विभागमन्त्रेण कर्णाम्̐श् चाकर्णाम्̐श्च तण्डुलान् विविचन्ति । क्षोदिष्ठाम्̐श् च स्थविष्ठाम्̐श् चेत्य् एकेषाम् ॥
13.4.22.a.m: At the time of pouring out the mess of boiled rice for Mitra, with the rule: 'Having poured out for Bṛhaspati, he pours out for Mitra', or, after they have been winnowed thrice, with the division formula they separate the grains with ears and without ears; the finest and the coarsest, according to some.

13.4.23.a.s: ye karṇāḥ sa payasi bārhaspatyaḥ / ye 'karṇāḥ sa ājye maitraḥ sa yadā śṛtaḥ syād atha taṃ maitrapātram upariṣṭād avadadhāti //
13.4.23.a.d: ये कर्णाः स पयसि बार्हस्पत्यः । ये ऽकर्णाः स आज्ये मैत्रः स यदा शृतः स्याद् अथ तं मैत्रपात्रम् उपरिष्टाद् अवदधाति ॥
13.4.23.a.m: Those which have ears are [cooked] in milk for Bṛhaspati; those which are without ears are [cooked] in clarified butter for Mitra. When it is cooked, then he places the vessel for Mitra upon it.

13.4.24.a.m: Having placed the two strainers in it, he pours the clarified butter that has melted of itself.

13.4.25.a.s: tasmin pavitravaty ājye sthavīyas taṇḍulān āvapati //
13.4.25.a.d: तस्मिन् पवित्रवत्य् आज्ये स्थवीयस् तण्डुलान् आवपति ॥
13.4.25.a.m: Into that clarified butter containing the strainers, he throws the coarser grains.

13.4.26.a.m: He cooks both together, the one above the other.

13.4.27.a.s: dharmamātram̐ śrapaṇam ardham̐ svayaṃdinaṃ barhiḥ svayaṃkṛta idhmo nimram adhyavasyati / sā svayaṃkṛtā vedir bhavati / vedyāḥ karoti / ardham̐ svayaṃkṛtaṃ bhavati / ardhaṃ barhiṣo dāti / ardhaṃ svayaṃdinam upasaṃnahyati / ardham idhmaṃ karoti //
13.4.27.a.d: धर्ममात्रम्̐ श्रपणम् अर्धम्̐ स्वयंदिनं बर्हिः स्वयंकृत इध्मो निम्रम् अध्यवस्यति । सा स्वयंकृता वेदिर् भवति । वेद्याः करोति । अर्धम्̐ स्वयंकृतं भवति । अर्धं बर्हिषो दाति । अर्धं स्वयंदिनम् उपसंनह्यति । अर्धम् इध्मं करोति ॥
13.4.27.a.m: The cooking is merely for heating. Half the sacred grass is fallen of itself; the firewood is formed of itself. He settles upon low ground; that becomes an altar formed of itself. He prepares it from the altar; half is formed of itself. He cuts half the sacred grass; he binds together half that is fallen of itself; he prepares half the firewood.

13.4.28.a.s: api vā svayaṃkṛtā vedir bhavati / saṃlobhya barhiḥ saṃcāryedhmaḥ //
13.4.28.a.d: अपि वा स्वयंकृता वेदिर् भवति । संलोभ्य बर्हिः संचार्येध्मः ॥
13.4.28.a.m: Or the altar is formed of itself; the sacred grass is mixed; the firewood is collected together.

13.4.29.a.m: At the time of the procedure, having performed the rite with the offering to Bṛhaspati, he performs the rite with the offering to Mitra.

13.4.30.a.s: itarathā vā / śitipṛṣṭho bārhaspatyasya dakṣiṇā / aśvo maitrasya / vyuptavaho vā / sā caiva śvetā śvetavatsā dakṣiṇā //
13.4.30.a.d: इतरथा वा । शितिपृष्ठो बार्हस्पत्यस्य दक्षिणा । अश्वो मैत्रस्य । व्युप्तवहो वा । सा चैव श्वेता श्वेतवत्सा दक्षिणा ॥
13.4.30.a.m: Or conversely. A white-backed [bull] is the sacrificial gift for that to Bṛhaspati; a horse for that to Mitra, or a draught ox, and that very white cow having a white calf is the sacrificial gift.

13.5.1.a.s: tathā dīkṣāḥ pravardhayanty abhiṣecanīyasya / yathā daśarātre śiṣṭe saṃvatsarasya daśapeyo bhaviṣyati //
13.5.1.a.d: तथा दीक्षाः प्रवर्धयन्त्य् अभिषेचनीयस्य । यथा दशरात्रे शिष्टे संवत्सरस्य दशपेयो भविष्यति ॥
13.5.1.a.m: They extend the consecrations of the consecratory rite in such a way that the Daśapeya will take place when ten nights of the year remain.

13.5.2.a.s: saha somau krīṇāti / abhiṣecanīyāya daśapeyāya cārdhaṃ rājñaḥ purohitasya brahmaṇo vā daśapeyārthaṃ nidadhāti //
13.5.2.a.d: सह सोमौ क्रीणाति । अभिषेचनीयाय दशपेयाय चार्धं राज्ञः पुरोहितस्य ब्रह्मणो वा दशपेयार्थं निदधाति ॥
13.5.2.a.m: He purchases the two somas together: for the consecratory rite and for the Daśapeya. He deposits half the king [soma] with the royal domestic priest or with the brahman priest for the sake of the Daśapeya.

13.5.3.a.s: agnīṣomīyapaśupuroḍāśaṃ nirupya devasuvām̐ havīm̐ṣy anunirvapati \\ agnaye gṛhapataye \\ iti yathāsamāmnātam / paśupuroḍāśasya devasuvāṃ ca haviṣām̐ samānam̐ sviṣṭakṛdiḍam //
13.5.3.a.d: अग्नीषोमीयपशुपुरोडाशं निरुप्य देवसुवाम्̐ हवीम्̐ष्य् अनुनिर्वपति \\ अग्नये गृहपतये \\ इति यथासमाम्नातम् । पशुपुरोडाशस्य देवसुवां च हविषाम्̐ समानम्̐ स्विष्टकृदिडम् ॥
13.5.3.a.m: Having poured out the animal sacrificial cake to Agni and Soma, he pours out following it the sacrificial oblations to the divine instigators, as handed down: 'To Agni, the lord of the house'. The animal sacrificial cake and the sacrificial oblations to the divine instigators have a common Sviṣṭakṛt offering and iḍā.

13.5.4.a.s: purastāt sviṣṭakṛtaḥ savitā tvā prasavānām̐ suvatām iti yajamānasya hastaṃ devayati \\ eṣa vaḥ kuravo rājā \\ iti / yadi kauravyaḥ / eṣa vaḥ pañcālā rājā \\ iti yady u vai pāñcālaḥ / eṣa vo bharatā rājā \\ iti vā kurupañcālān eṣa te janatā rājā \\ ity anyān rājñaḥ / somo 'smākaṃ brāhmaṇānām̐ rājā \\ ity ukte //
13.5.4.a.d: पुरस्तात् स्विष्टकृतः सविता त्वा प्रसवानाम्̐ सुवताम् इति यजमानस्य हस्तं देवयति \\ एष वः कुरवो राजा \\ इति । यदि कौरव्यः । एष वः पञ्चाला राजा \\ इति यद्य् उ वै पाञ्चालः । एष वो भरता राजा \\ इति वा कुरुपञ्चालान् एष ते जनता राजा \\ इत्य् अन्यान् राज्ञः । सोमो ऽस्माकं ब्राह्मणानाम्̐ राजा \\ इत्य् उक्ते ॥
13.5.4.a.m: Before the Sviṣṭakṛt offering, he raises the sacrificer's hand with: 'May Savitṛ impel you of the impellings'. With: 'This is your king, O Kurus!', if he is a Kauravya. With: 'This is your king, O Pañcālas!', if he is a Pāñcāla. Or with: 'This is your king, O Bharatas!', for the Kuru-Pañcālas; with: 'This is your king, O people!', for other kings. When it has been spoken: 'Soma is the king of us brāhmaṇas',

13.5.5.a.s: prati tyan nāma rājyam adhāyi \\ iti vāruṇībhyāṃ yajamāno mukhaṃ vimṛṣṭe //
13.5.5.a.d: प्रति त्यन् नाम राज्यम् अधायि \\ इति वारुणीभ्यां यजमानो मुखं विमृष्टे ॥
13.5.5.a.m: With two verses addressed to Varuṇa, beginning: 'Unto him indeed kingship has been established', the sacrificer wipes his face.

13.5.6.a.s: viṣṇoḥ kramo 'si \\ iti trīn viṣṇukramān prācaḥ krāmati //
13.5.6.a.d: विष्णोः क्रमो ऽसि \\ इति त्रीन् विष्णुक्रमान् प्राचः क्रामति ॥
13.5.6.a.m: With: 'You are the stride of Viṣṇu', he strides three Viṣṇu-strides towards the east.

13.5.7.a.s: yat prāṅ māhendrāt tasmin kṛte pratiprasthātā mārutam ekavim̐śatikapālaṃ nirvapati //
13.5.7.a.d: यत् प्राङ् माहेन्द्रात् तस्मिन् कृते प्रतिप्रस्थाता मारुतम् एकविम्̐शतिकपालं निर्वपति ॥
13.5.7.a.m: When that which precedes the Māhendra cup has been done, the pratiprasthātā pours out an offering to the Maruts on twenty-one potsherds.

13.5.8.a.m: He lays down the potsherds in troops.

13.5.9.a.s: āraṇyenānuvākyena gaṇe madhya upadhāyāmikṣāyāḥ kalpena maitrāvaruṇīm āmikṣāṃ karoti //
13.5.9.a.d: आरण्येनानुवाक्येन गणे मध्य उपधायामिक्षायाः कल्पेन मैत्रावरुणीम् आमिक्षां करोति ॥
13.5.9.a.m: Having placed the potsherd in the middle of the troop with the forest introductory verse, he prepares the curd-mixture to Mitra and Varuṇa according to the procedure of the curd-mixture.

13.5.10.a.m: He takes the drawing of waters with cups for Vāyu that have been kept overnight.

13.5.11.a.s: devīr āpo apāṃnapād rāṣṭradā stha \ rāṣṭraṃ datta svāhā \\ iti sārasvatīṣv apsu hutvaitenaiva gṛhṇāti //
13.5.11.a.d: देवीर् आपो अपांनपाद् राष्ट्रदा स्थ \ राष्ट्रं दत्त स्वाहा \\ इति सारस्वतीष्व् अप्सु हुत्वैतेनैव गृह्णाति ॥
13.5.11.a.m: Having offered into the waters of the Sarasvatī with: 'O divine waters, offspring of the waters, you are kingdom-givers; give the kingdom, svāhā!', he draws [water] with this very formula.

13.5.12.a.s: arthetaḥ stha \\ iti vā / evam itarāsu yenayena juhoti tenatena gṛhṇāti //
13.5.12.a.d: अर्थेतः स्थ \\ इति वा । एवम् इतरासु येनयेन जुहोति तेनतेन गृह्णाति ॥
13.5.12.a.m: Or with: 'You have come with a purpose'. Likewise with the other [waters]: with whichever [formula] he makes the offering, with that he draws [the water].

13.5.13.a.s: rāṣṭradāḥ stha \ rāṣṭraṃ datta svāhā \\ iti homārthe 'nuṣajati / rāṣṭradāḥ stha \ rāṣṭram amuṣmai datta \\ iti gṛhṇāti //
13.5.13.a.d: राष्ट्रदाः स्थ \ राष्ट्रं दत्त स्वाहा \\ इति होमार्थे ऽनुषजति । राष्ट्रदाः स्थ \ राष्ट्रम् अमुष्मै दत्त \\ इति गृह्णाति ॥
13.5.13.a.m: For the purpose of offering, he appends: 'You are granters of realm; grant realm, svāhā!'; he takes [the waters] with: 'You are granters of realm; grant realm to so-and-so!'

13.5.14.a.s: puruṣe yaśau vābhyavete \\ apāṃ patir asi \\ iti // samudriyāḥ saindhavīr vā pratīpam anya ūrmiḥ patati / anvīpam anyas \\ vṛṣāsy ūrmis \\ iti yaḥ pratīpaṃ taṃ gṛhṇāti / vṛṣaseno 'si \\ iti yo 'nvīpam / prahāvarīḥ stha \\ iti sthāvarāṇām / yāḥ sthānaṃ na pravahanti parivāhiṇīḥ stha \\ iti sravantīnām / yā āpa uccherate pariṇatiṃ bruvate / vrajakṣitaḥ stha \\ iti kūpyānām / marutām ojasaḥ stha \\ iti hrādunīnām / sūryavarcasaḥ stha \\ ity ātapativarṣyāṇām / sūryatvacasaḥ stha \\ iti yāsu rūpāṇi paridṛśyante / māndāḥ stha \\ iti sthāvarāṇāṃ yā vā mandam iva syandante / vāśāḥ stha \\ iti pṛṣṭhānām / śakvarī stha \\ iti gor ulbyānām / viśvabhṛtaḥ stha \\ iti payasaḥ / janabhṛtaḥ stha \\ iti dadhnaḥ / agnes tejasyāḥ stha \\ iti ghṛtasya / śraviṣṭhāḥ stha \\ anādhṛṣṭās \\ iti vā / apām oṣadhīnām̐ rasaḥ stha \\ iti madhunaḥ ṣoḍaśa saptadaśa vā gṛhṇāti //
13.5.14.a.d: पुरुषे यशौ वाभ्यवेते \\ अपां पतिर् असि \\ इति ॥ समुद्रियाः सैन्धवीर् वा प्रतीपम् अन्य ऊर्मिः पतति । अन्वीपम् अन्यस् \\ वृषास्य् ऊर्मिस् \\ इति यः प्रतीपं तं गृह्णाति । वृषसेनो ऽसि \\ इति यो ऽन्वीपम् । प्रहावरीः स्थ \\ इति स्थावराणाम् । याः स्थानं न प्रवहन्ति परिवाहिणीः स्थ \\ इति स्रवन्तीनाम् । या आप उच्छेरते परिणतिं ब्रुवते । व्रजक्षितः स्थ \\ इति कूप्यानाम् । मरुताम् ओजसः स्थ \\ इति ह्रादुनीनाम् । सूर्यवर्चसः स्थ \\ इत्य् आतपतिवर्ष्याणाम् । सूर्यत्वचसः स्थ \\ इति यासु रूपाणि परिदृश्यन्ते । मान्दाः स्थ \\ इति स्थावराणां या वा मन्दम् इव स्यन्दन्ते । वाशाः स्थ \\ इति पृष्ठानाम् । शक्वरी स्थ \\ इति गोर् उल्ब्यानाम् । विश्वभृतः स्थ \\ इति पयसः । जनभृतः स्थ \\ इति दध्नः । अग्नेस् तेजस्याः स्थ \\ इति घृतस्य । श्रविष्ठाः स्थ \\ अनाधृष्टास् \\ इति वा । अपाम् ओषधीनाम्̐ रसः स्थ \\ इति मधुनः षोडश सप्तदश वा गृह्णाति ॥
13.5.14.a.m: When a man or two persons of renown step into [the water, he takes it] with: 'You are the lord of the waters'; waters of the sea or of the Sindhu; one wave breaks against the current, another with the current: with 'You are a vigorous wave', he takes the one which [breaks] against the current; with 'You are a vigorous host', that which [breaks] with the current; with 'You are the moving ones', [water] from standing waters; with 'You are the flowing ones', [water] from running waters which do not flow [away from their] place; waters which surge up and swirl around; with 'You are dwelling in the stall', [water] from wells; with 'You are the vigor of the Maruts', [water] from thunder-clouds; with 'You possess the radiance of the sun', [water from rain] falling while the sun shines; with 'You possess the skin of the sun', [water] in which forms are clearly reflected; with 'You are sluggish', [water] from standing waters, or which flow as if slowly; with 'You are lowing ones', [water] from the surface; with 'You are mighty', [water] from the amniotic fluid of a cow; with 'You are all-supporting', [he takes] milk; with 'You are people-supporting', curd; with 'You possess the splendor of Agni', clarified butter; with 'You are most famous', or with 'unconquered', with 'You are the essence of waters and plants', [he takes] honey; he takes sixteen or seventeen [types of waters].

13.5.15.a.s: apo devīr madhumatīr agṛhṇan \\ iti gṛhītvābhimantrayate //
13.5.15.a.d: अपो देवीर् मधुमतीर् अगृह्णन् \\ इति गृहीत्वाभिमन्त्रयते ॥
13.5.15.a.m: Having taken [them], he consecrates them with: 'The divine, honey-filled waters have they taken...'

13.5.16.a.s: devīr āpaḥ saṃ madhumatīr madhumatībhiḥ sṛjyadhvam iti vaitase droṇe samavanayati //
13.5.16.a.d: देवीर् आपः सं मधुमतीर् मधुमतीभिः सृज्यध्वम् इति वैतसे द्रोणे समवनयति ॥
13.5.16.a.m: He pours them together into a cane trough with: 'O divine waters, honey-filled, unite with the honey-filled ones!'

13.5.17.a.m: Some teach the recitation of the consecration at this point.

13.5.18.a.s: anādhṛṣṭāḥ sīdata \\ ity antarā hotur dhiṣṇiyaṃ brāhmaṇāccham̐sinaś ca sādayati //
13.5.18.a.d: अनाधृष्टाः सीदत \\ इत्य् अन्तरा होतुर् धिष्णियं ब्राह्मणाच्छम्̐सिनश् च सादयति ॥
13.5.18.a.m: He deposits [the waters] between the dhiṣṇiya hearths of the hotṛ and the brāhmaṇācchaṃsin with: 'Sit down, unconquered!'

13.5.19.a.m: According to some, he places them behind the hotrīya hearth.

13.5.20.a.s: anibhṛṣṭam asi \\ iti śatātṛṇṇam̐ sauvarṇam̐ rukmam ādāya śukrā vaḥ śukreṇotpunāmi \\ iti tena trir utpunāti //
13.5.20.a.d: अनिभृष्टम् असि \\ इति शतातृण्णम्̐ सौवर्णम्̐ रुक्मम् आदाय शुक्रा वः शुक्रेणोत्पुनामि \\ इति तेन त्रिर् उत्पुनाति ॥
13.5.20.a.m: With [the mantra,] “You are unbroken,” taking a golden plate perforated with a hundred holes, he purifies three times through it with [the mantra,] “Being bright, I purify you with the bright one.”

13.5.21.a.s: sadhamādo dyumninīr ūrja etās \\ iti caturṣu pātreṣu vyānayati // pālāśa audumbara āśvatthe naiyagrodhe 'vaśeṣaṃ droṇe karoti //
13.5.21.a.d: सधमादो द्युम्निनीर् ऊर्ज एतास् \\ इति चतुर्षु पात्रेषु व्यानयति ॥ पालाश औदुम्बर आश्वत्थे नैयग्रोधे ऽवशेषं द्रोणे करोति ॥
13.5.21.a.m: With [the mantra,] “These invigorating, glorious rejoicers together,” he pours out [the unction water] into four vessels: one of palāśa wood, one of udumbara wood, one of aśvattha wood, and one of nyagrodha wood; he puts the remainder into a wooden trough.

13.5.22.a.m: He feeds the sacrificer young sprouted barley, udumbara [fruit], and curd.

13.5.23.a.s: ekaśatena darbhapuñjīlair āṅkte / śatenety ekeṣām / pañcāśatā dakṣiṇam akṣy ekapañcāśatottaram abhyajya kṣatrasyolbam asi \\ iti tṛpāṇāṃ vṛkṣāṇāṃ vāso yajamānaḥ paridhatte / kṣatrasya yonir asi \\ iti pāṇḍuram uṣṇīṣam / tṛtīyam̐ śvetapāṇḍuram ity ācakṣate / apa upasparśayitvā \\ āvinno agnir ity āvido yajamānaṃ vācayan bahiḥsadasam abhyudānayati //
13.5.23.a.d: एकशतेन दर्भपुञ्जीलैर् आङ्क्ते । शतेनेत्य् एकेषाम् । पञ्चाशता दक्षिणम् अक्ष्य् एकपञ्चाशतोत्तरम् अभ्यज्य क्षत्रस्योल्बम् असि \\ इति तृपाणां वृक्षाणां वासो यजमानः परिधत्ते । क्षत्रस्य योनिर् असि \\ इति पाण्डुरम् उष्णीषम् । तृतीयम्̐ श्वेतपाण्डुरम् इत्य् आचक्षते । अप उपस्पर्शयित्वा \\ आविन्नो अग्निर् इत्य् आविदो यजमानं वाचयन् बहिःसदसम् अभ्युदानयति ॥
13.5.23.a.m: With one hundred and one darbha stalks he anoints [his eyes]; “with a hundred,” say some. Having anointed the right eye with fifty and the left with fifty-one, the sacrificer puts on a garment woven of bark with [the mantra,] “You are the womb of royal power.” With [the mantra,] “You are the source of royal power,” [he puts on] a pale turban; “a third [cloth] is a white-and-pale one,” they say. Having made him touch water, causing the sacrificer to recite the proclamation formulas starting with “Agni is proclaimed,” he leads him out toward the front of the sadas.

13.5.24.a.s: eṣa vaḥ kuravo rājā \\ ity āvedayati / manasānuprakrāmati / manasordhvam anūjjihīte //
13.5.24.a.d: एष वः कुरवो राजा \\ इत्य् आवेदयति । मनसानुप्रक्रामति । मनसोर्ध्वम् अनूज्जिहीते ॥
13.5.24.a.m: “This, O Kurus, is your king,” he proclaims. He steps forward mentally; he stands upward mentally.

13.5.25.a.m: At this point some prescribe a cake on twenty-one potsherds for the Maruts.

13.5.26.a.s: somasya tviṣir asi \ taveva me tviṣir bhūyāt \\ iti śārdūlacarma viveṣṭayati //
13.5.26.a.d: सोमस्य त्विषिर् असि \ तवेव मे त्विषिर् भूयात् \\ इति शार्दूलचर्म विवेष्टयति ॥
13.5.26.a.m: With [the mantra,] “You are the brilliance of Soma; may my brilliance be like yours,” he rolls out a tiger skin.

13.5.27.a.s: agre sado dakṣiṇe dvārabāhau tad yajamāna ārohati / aveṣṭā dandaśūkās \\ iti / āpaḥ keśavāpāya prayacchati // lohāyasaṃ prayacchatīty ekeṣām //
13.5.27.a.d: अग्रे सदो दक्षिणे द्वारबाहौ तद् यजमान आरोहति । अवेष्टा दन्दशूकास् \\ इति । आपः केशवापाय प्रयच्छति ॥ लोहायसं प्रयच्छतीत्य् एकेषाम् ॥
13.5.27.a.m: In front of the sadas, by the right door-post, the sacrificer steps upon it with [the mantra,] “The biting serpents are dispelled.” He gives water to the barber; “he gives bronze,” say some.

13.5.28.a.s: nirastaṃ namuceḥ śiras \\ iti sīsaṃ klībāya vidhyati cainam̐ sīsaṃ klībena vidhyatīty ekeṣām //
13.5.28.a.d: निरस्तं नमुचेः शिरस् \\ इति सीसं क्लीबाय विध्यति चैनम्̐ सीसं क्लीबेन विध्यतीत्य् एकेषाम् ॥
13.5.28.a.m: With [the mantra,] “The head of Namuci is cast away,” he throws a lead [token] to a eunuch; and some say, “he shoots him with a lead [token] through a eunuch.”

13.5.29.a.s: pratyastaṃ namuceḥ śiras \\ iti vāpa upaspṛśya //
13.5.29.a.d: प्रत्यस्तं नमुचेः शिरस् \\ इति वाप उपस्पृश्य ॥
13.5.29.a.m: Having touched water with [the mantra,] “The head of Namuci is cast back”;

13.5.30.a.s: amṛtam asi \\ iti rajatam̐ rukmaṃ vyāghracarmaṇy upohati / adhastāt pādayor didyon mā pāhi \\ iti śatātṛṇṇam̐ sauvarṇam̐ rukmaṃ yajamānasya śirasi nidadhāti //
13.5.30.a.d: अमृतम् असि \\ इति रजतम्̐ रुक्मं व्याघ्रचर्मण्य् उपोहति । अधस्तात् पादयोर् दिद्योन् मा पाहि \\ इति शतातृण्णम्̐ सौवर्णम्̐ रुक्मं यजमानस्य शिरसि निदधाति ॥
13.5.30.a.m: with [the mantra,] “You are immortal,” he slips a silver plate under the tiger skin under [the sacrificer's] feet; with [the mantra,] “Protect me from lightning,” he places a golden plate perforated with a hundred holes upon the sacrificer's head.

13.5.31.a.s: somo rājā varuṇas \\ ity etābhyo devatābhyaḥ procya \\ agnaye svāhā \\ iti ṣaṭ pūrvāṇi pārthāni hutvā pṛthivyai svāhā \\ iti ṣaṭ pūrvā bhūtānām aveṣṭīr juhoti //
13.5.31.a.d: सोमो राजा वरुणस् \\ इत्य् एताभ्यो देवताभ्यः प्रोच्य \\ अग्नये स्वाहा \\ इति षट् पूर्वाणि पार्थानि हुत्वा पृथिव्यै स्वाहा \\ इति षट् पूर्वा भूतानाम् अवेष्टीर् जुहोति ॥
13.5.31.a.m: Having announced to these deities with [the mantra,] “King Soma, Varuṇa…,” and having offered the first six Pārtha offerings with “To Agni, svāhā,” he offers the first six Aveṣṭi offerings of creatures with “To the earth, svāhā.”

13.5.32.a.s: somasya tvā dyumnenābhiṣiñcāmi \\ ity adhvaryur vāhutiṃ juhūm̐ hūyamāne 'bhiṣiñcati //
13.5.32.a.d: सोमस्य त्वा द्युम्नेनाभिषिञ्चामि \\ इत्य् अध्वर्युर् वाहुतिं जुहूम्̐ हूयमाने ऽभिषिञ्चति ॥
13.5.32.a.m: With [the mantra,] “I consecrate you with the brilliance of Soma,” the adhvaryu—or [another]—consecrates him while the oblation is being offered into the juhū.

13.5.33.a.s: parṇamayena purastād adhvaryuḥ / evam itare / audumbareṇa dakṣiṇato brahmā / rājanyo vā / āśvatthena paścād vaiśyaḥ / naiyagrodhenottarato janyamitram / syād upariṣṭāddevanasyāsiñcati //
13.5.33.a.d: पर्णमयेन पुरस्ताद् अध्वर्युः । एवम् इतरे । औदुम्बरेण दक्षिणतो ब्रह्मा । राजन्यो वा । आश्वत्थेन पश्चाद् वैश्यः । नैयग्रोधेनोत्तरतो जन्यमित्रम् । स्याद् उपरिष्टाद्देवनस्यासिञ्चति ॥
13.5.33.a.m: The adhvaryu [consecrates] from the east with the palāśa vessel; likewise the others: the brahman—or a noble—from the south with the udumbara vessel; a vaiśya from the west with the aśvattha vessel; a friend of the people from the north with the nyagrodha vessel; or he pours it over the gaming-board.

13.5.34.a.s: kṣatrāṇāṃ kṣatrapatir asi \\ ity abhiṣicyamānam abhimantrayate //
13.5.34.a.d: क्षत्राणां क्षत्रपतिर् असि \\ इत्य् अभिषिच्यमानम् अभिमन्त्रयते ॥
13.5.34.a.m: He addresses [the sacrificer] being consecrated with [the mantra,] “You are the lord of royal powers among royal powers.”

13.5.35.a.s: ati divas pāhi \\ iti kṛṣṇaviṣāṇayā rājasūyikāni vāsām̐si vivṛtya samāvavṛtrann adharāg udīcīs \\ iti ye 'bhiṣicyamānasya lepā vyavasravanti / tān pātraiḥ samunmārṣṭi //
13.5.35.a.d: अति दिवस् पाहि \\ इति कृष्णविषाणया राजसूयिकानि वासाम्̐सि विवृत्य समाववृत्रन्न् अधराग् उदीचीस् \\ इति ये ऽभिषिच्यमानस्य लेपा व्यवस्रवन्ति । तान् पात्रैः समुन्मार्ष्टि ॥
13.5.35.a.m: With [the mantra,] “Protect [me] from heaven,” having unfolded the Rājasūya garments with a black antelope horn, with [the mantra,] “They have turned together, backward and upward,” he wipes together with the vessels the residues that flow down from the consecrated [sacrificer].

13.5.36.a.s: indrāya svāhā \\ iti ṣaḍ uttarāṇi pārthāni hutvā \\ adbhyaḥ svāhā \\ iti ṣaḍ uttarā bhūtānām aveṣṭīr juhoti //
13.5.36.a.d: इन्द्राय स्वाहा \\ इति षड् उत्तराणि पार्थानि हुत्वा \\ अद्भ्यः स्वाहा \\ इति षड् उत्तरा भूतानाम् अवेष्टीर् जुहोति ॥
13.5.36.a.m: Having offered the last six Pārtha offerings with “To Indra, svāhā,” he offers the last six Aveṣṭi offerings of creatures with “To the waters, svāhā.”

13.5.37.a.s: rudra yat te krayī paraṃ nāma \\ iti yo droṇe śeṣas tam udaṅ paretyāgnīdhre juhoti //
13.5.37.a.d: रुद्र यत् ते क्रयी परं नाम \\ इति यो द्रोणे शेषस् तम् उदङ् परेत्याग्नीध्रे जुहोति ॥
13.5.37.a.m: Going north, he offers whatever remains in the wooden trough into the āgnīdhra fire with [the mantra,] “O Rudra, that purchasing, supreme name of yours…”

13.6.1.a.s: indrasya vajro 'si vārtraghnas \\ iti ratham upāvaharati //
13.6.1.a.d: इन्द्रस्य वज्रो ऽसि वार्त्रघ्नस् \\ इति रथम् उपावहरति ॥
13.6.1.a.m: With [the mantra,] “You are Indra's thunderbolt, the slayer of Vṛtra,” he brings down the chariot.

13.6.2.a.s: mitrāvaruṇayos tvā praśāstroḥ praśiṣā yunajmi \\ iti praṣṭivāhinam̐ rathaṃ yunakti //
13.6.2.a.d: मित्रावरुणयोस् त्वा प्रशास्त्रोः प्रशिषा युनज्मि \\ इति प्रष्टिवाहिनम्̐ रथं युनक्ति ॥
13.6.2.a.m: With [the mantra,] “I yoke you by the command of Mitra and Varuṇa, the commanders,” he yokes the chariot drawn by a side-horse.

13.6.3.a.d: विष्णोः क्रमो ऽसि \\ इति रथम् आतिष्ठति ॥
13.6.3.a.m: With [the mantra,] “You are the stride of Viṣṇu,” he steps onto the chariot.

13.6.4.a.m: With [the mantra,] “May I conquer in the instigation of the Maruts,” he drives forward.

13.6.5.a.m: With [the verse,] “You have conquered,” the brahman follows from the south with a triṣṭubh verse.

13.6.6.a.m: “The appointed one takes hold of it from behind,” say some.

13.6.7.a.s: sadhanū rājanyaḥ purastād uttarato vāvasthito bhavati //
13.6.7.a.d: सधनू राजन्यः पुरस्ताद् उत्तरतो वावस्थितो भवति ॥
13.6.7.a.m: A noble with a bow stands in front or to the north.

13.6.8.a.s: taṃ jināti \\ āptaṃ manaḥ \ sam aham indriyeṇa \\ iti //
13.6.8.a.d: तं जिनाति \\ आप्तं मनः \ सम् अहम् इन्द्रियेण \\ इति ॥
13.6.8.a.m: He overpowers him with [the mantra,] “The mind is attained; together am I with power.”

13.6.9.a.s: tasmā etān iṣūn asyati prati tvāptaṃ manaḥ \ sam aham indriyeṇa \\ iti pradakṣiṇam āvartate //
13.6.9.a.d: तस्मा एतान् इषून् अस्यति प्रति त्वाप्तं मनः \ सम् अहम् इन्द्रियेण \\ इति प्रदक्षिणम् आवर्तते ॥
13.6.9.a.m: He shoots these arrows at him; with [the mantra,] “Mind is attained against you; together am I with power,” he turns clockwise.

13.6.10.a.s: eṣa vajro vājasātamas tena tau putrau vājasam̐ set \\ iti dhanuḥ patnyai prayacchati / dhanurārtniṃ prayacchatīty ekeṣām / patnī dhanurārjño 'panudatīty ekeṣām / aśvān upaspṛśatīty ekeṣām //
13.6.10.a.d: एष वज्रो वाजसातमस् तेन तौ पुत्रौ वाजसम्̐ सेत् \\ इति धनुः पत्न्यै प्रयच्छति । धनुरार्त्निं प्रयच्छतीत्य् एकेषाम् । पत्नी धनुरार्ज्ञो ऽपनुदतीत्य् एकेषाम् । अश्वान् उपस्पृशतीत्य् एकेषाम् ॥
13.6.10.a.m: With [the mantra,] “This is the thunderbolt, best at winning booty; through it may those two sons win booty,” he hands the bow to the wife; “he hands the bow-notch,” say some; “the wife pushes away the two bow-ends,” say some; “he touches the horses,” say some.

13.6.11.a.s: iyad asi \\ āyur asi \\ āyur me dhehi \\ iti rājatamaṇiṃ yajamānaḥ pratimuñcate // ūrg asi \\ ity audumbaram / yuṅṅ asi \\ iti sauvarṇam //
13.6.11.a.d: इयद् असि \\ आयुर् असि \\ आयुर् मे धेहि \\ इति राजतमणिं यजमानः प्रतिमुञ्चते ॥ ऊर्ग् असि \\ इत्य् औदुम्बरम् । युङ्ङ् असि \\ इति सौवर्णम् ॥
13.6.11.a.m: The sacrificer fastens on a silver bead with [the mantra,] “You are this much; you are life; bestow life upon me”; a bead of udumbara wood with [the mantra,] “You are vigor”; a golden one with [the mantra,] “You are the yoker.”

13.6.12.a.m: Some prescribe the golden one in the middle.

13.6.13.a.s: mitro 'si \\ iti dakṣiṇaṃ bāhum upāvaharate / varuṇo 'si \\ iti savyam / etad vā viparītam //
13.6.13.a.d: मित्रो ऽसि \\ इति दक्षिणं बाहुम् उपावहरते । वरुणो ऽसि \\ इति सव्यम् । एतद् वा विपरीतम् ॥
13.6.13.a.m: With [the mantra,] “You are Mitra,” he brings down his right arm; with [the mantra,] “You are Varuṇa,” his left; or the reverse of this.

13.6.14.a.s: sam ahaṃ viśvair devais \\ iti vaiśvadevyām āmikṣāyām̐ hastāv upāvaharate / atraite hiraṇye dadāti sauvarṇam̐ rājataṃ ca maṇim //
13.6.14.a.d: सम् अहं विश्वैर् देवैस् \\ इति वैश्वदेव्याम् आमिक्षायाम्̐ हस्ताव् उपावहरते । अत्रैते हिरण्ये ददाति सौवर्णम्̐ राजतं च मणिम् ॥
13.6.14.a.m: With [the mantra,] “Together am I with all the gods,” he lowers his two hands into the curd-mixture for the Viśvedevas; at this point he gives these two gold pieces: the golden and the silver beads.

13.6.15.a.s: namo mātre pṛthivyai \\ ity avarohan pṛthivīm avekṣate // paśūnāṃ manyur asi \ taveva me manyur bhūyāt \\ iti vārāhī upānahāv adhyavarohati //
13.6.15.a.d: नमो मात्रे पृथिव्यै \\ इत्य् अवरोहन् पृथिवीम् अवेक्षते ॥ पशूनां मन्युर् असि \ तवेव मे मन्युर् भूयात् \\ इति वाराही उपानहाव् अध्यवरोहति ॥
13.6.15.a.m: Stepping down with [the mantra,] “Homage to Mother Earth,” he looks at the earth; with [the mantra,] “You are the wrath of the beasts; may my wrath be like yours,” he steps down onto boar-skin sandals.

13.6.16.a.s: prati tyan nāma rājyam adhāyi \\ iti vāruṇībhyāṃ mukhaṃ vimṛṣṭe //
13.6.16.a.d: प्रति त्यन् नाम राज्यम् अधायि \\ इति वारुणीभ्यां मुखं विमृष्टे ॥
13.6.16.a.m: With [the mantra,] “The famous kingship has been established,” he wipes his face with two Varuṇa verses.

13.6.17.a.s: agreṇāgnīdhraṃ caturavastāvaṃ kharaṃ vimitaṃ viminvanti / dakṣiṇata upacāram \\ kṣatrasya nābhir asi \\ iti tasmin khādirīm āsandīṃ pratiṣṭhāpayati / kṣatrasya yonir asi \\ iti tasyāṃ kṛttyadhīvāsam āstṛṇāti //
13.6.17.a.d: अग्रेणाग्नीध्रं चतुरवस्तावं खरं विमितं विमिन्वन्ति । दक्षिणत उपचारम् \\ क्षत्रस्य नाभिर् असि \\ इति तस्मिन् खादिरीम् आसन्दीं प्रतिष्ठापयति । क्षत्रस्य योनिर् असि \\ इति तस्यां कृत्त्यधीवासम् आस्तृणाति ॥
13.6.17.a.m: In front of the āgnīdhra fire they erect a square, four-pegged shed with an entrance from the south; on it he sets up a chair made of khadira wood with [the mantra,] “You are the navel of royal power”; with [the mantra,] “You are the source of royal power,” he spreads a skin coverlet over it.

13.6.18.a.s: avanahyati hani viśi mā dṛm̐ha \\ ity avanahyati //
13.6.18.a.d: अवनह्यति हनि विशि मा दृम्̐ह \\ इत्य् अवनह्यति ॥
13.6.18.a.m: He ties it down; with [the mantra,] “O killer, make me firm among the people,” he ties it down.

13.6.20.a.s: syonām āsīda \ suṣadām āsīda \\ iti sīdantam abhimantrayate //
13.6.20.a.d: स्योनाम् आसीद \ सुषदाम् आसीद \\ इति सीदन्तम् अभिमन्त्रयते ॥
13.6.20.a.m: He addresses him as he sits down with [the mantra,] “Sit down on the pleasant one; sit down on the one easy to sit upon.”

13.6.21.a.m: With [the mantra,] “May it not harm you,” he mounts [the chair].

13.6.22.a.s: mā tvā him̐sīt \\ mā mā him̐sīt \\ ity ārohantam abhimantrayate //
13.6.22.a.d: मा त्वा हिम्̐सीत् \\ मा मा हिम्̐सीत् \\ इत्य् आरोहन्तम् अभिमन्त्रयते ॥
13.6.22.a.m: He addresses him as he mounts with [the mantra,] “May it not harm you; may it not harm me.”

13.6.23.a.m: Seated, he mutters [the verse,] “He sat down, steadfast in his vows…”

13.6.24.a.s: agnaye gṛhapataye svāhā \\ iti sruveṇa gārhapatye rathavimocanīyāni hutvā ham̐saḥ śuciṣat \\ iti sahasaṃgrahītrā rathavāhane ratham ādadhāti //
13.6.24.a.d: अग्नये गृहपतये स्वाहा \\ इति स्रुवेण गार्हपत्ये रथविमोचनीयानि हुत्वा हम्̐सः शुचिषत् \\ इति सहसंग्रहीत्रा रथवाहने रथम् आदधाति ॥
13.6.24.a.m: Having offered the chariot-unloosing oblations into the gārhapatya fire with the dipping spoon, with “To Agni, the lord of the house, svāhā,” he places the chariot on the chariot-stand together with the charioteer with [the verse,] “The swan seated in the clear…”

13.6.25.a.s: āhite saṃgrahītāvarohati ṛtvijo ratninaś ca rājānaṃ paryupaviśante samupaviṣṭeṣu brahmā3n ity adhvaryuṃ yajamāna āmantrayate / tvam̐ rājan brahmāsi \ savitāsi satyasavas \\ iti pratyāhaivam̐ hotāraṃ brahmāṇam udgātāraṃ vāmantrayate / uttareṇottareṇa mantreṇa pratyāhuḥ //
13.6.25.a.d: आहिते संग्रहीतावरोहति ऋत्विजो रत्निनश् च राजानं पर्युपविशन्ते समुपविष्टेषु ब्रह्मा3न् इत्य् अध्वर्युं यजमान आमन्त्रयते । त्वम्̐ राजन् ब्रह्मासि \ सवितासि सत्यसवस् \\ इति प्रत्याहैवम्̐ होतारं ब्रह्माणम् उद्गातारं वामन्त्रयते । उत्तरेणोत्तरेण मन्त्रेण प्रत्याहुः ॥
13.6.25.a.m: When it has been placed, the charioteer steps down; the officiating priests and the royal jewels (dignitaries) sit down around the king; when they are seated together, the sacrificer addresses the adhvaryu: “O brāhman!”; he replies: “You, O King, are brahman; you are Savitṛ of true impulse”; in the same way he addresses the hotṛ, the brahman, or the udgātṛ; they reply each with the subsequent mantra.

13.6.26.a.s: indrasya vajro 'si vārtraghnas \\ iti sphyaṃ brahmātha rājñe prayacchati / adhvaryuḥ prayacchatīty ekeṣām //
13.6.26.a.d: इन्द्रस्य वज्रो ऽसि वार्त्रघ्नस् \\ इति स्फ्यं ब्रह्माथ राज्ञे प्रयच्छति । अध्वर्युः प्रयच्छतीत्य् एकेषाम् ॥
13.6.26.a.m: With [the mantra,] “You are Indra's thunderbolt, the slayer of Vṛtra,” the brahman then hands the wooden sword to the king; “the adhvaryu hands it,” say some.

13.6.27.a.s: eṣa vajro 'si vājasātamaḥ // \ tena me radhya \\ iti vā rājā purohitāya / purohitaḥ pratihitāya / pratihito ratnibhyas tam avaraparam̐ saṃprayacchanti / antato 'kṣāvāpāya prayacchati //
13.6.27.a.d: एष वज्रो ऽसि वाजसातमः ॥ \ तेन मे रध्य \\ इति वा राजा पुरोहिताय । पुरोहितः प्रतिहिताय । प्रतिहितो रत्निभ्यस् तम् अवरपरम्̐ संप्रयच्छन्ति । अन्ततो ऽक्षावापाय प्रयच्छति ॥
13.6.27.a.m: With: "This thunderbolt are you, most winning of spoils; / yield to me therewith," the king [gives the wooden sword] to the purohita; the purohita to the pratihita; the pratihita to the ratnins. They pass it down one after the other; in the end he gives it to the akṣāvāpa.

13.6.28.a.s: tena sa sphyenādhidevanam uddhatya tisraḥ pañcāśataḥ pañca vā pañcāśato 'kṣān nivapati //
13.6.28.a.d: तेन स स्फ्येनाधिदेवनम् उद्धत्य तिस्रः पञ्चाशतः पञ्च वा पञ्चाशतो ऽक्षान् निवपति ॥
13.6.28.a.m: With that wooden sword, having prepared the gambling place, he pours out three [sets of] fifty, or five [sets of] fifty dice.

13.6.29.a.s: udbhinnam̐ rājñas \\ iti tataś caturo 'kṣān nirūham̐ś catuḥśatān apisṛjya paṣṭhauhīṃ vidīvyanti //
13.6.29.a.d: उद्भिन्नम्̐ राज्ञस् \\ इति ततश् चतुरो ऽक्षान् निरूहम्̐श् चतुःशतान् अपिसृज्य पष्ठौहीं विदीव्यन्ति ॥
13.6.29.a.m: With: "Arisen is the king's [victory]," taking out four dice from them and having pushed aside the four sets, they play for a four-year-old cow.

13.6.30.a.s: brāhmaṇo rājanyo vaiśyaḥ śūdra ity odanam adhipaṇaṃ vijitya diśo 'bhy ayam̐ rājābhūt \\ iti pañcākṣān yajamānāya prayacchati //
13.6.30.a.d: ब्राह्मणो राजन्यो वैश्यः शूद्र इत्य् ओदनम् अधिपणं विजित्य दिशो ऽभ्य् अयम्̐ राजाभूत् \\ इति पञ्चाक्षान् यजमानाय प्रयच्छति ॥
13.6.30.a.m: Having won the boiled rice stakes—"a brāhmaṇa, a rājanya, a vaiśya, a śūdra"—with: "Towards the quarters has this king turned," he gives five dice to the sacrificer.

13.6.31.a.s: tānapisṛjya maṅgalyanāmno hvayati suślokā3m̐ iti saṃgrahītāram̐ asumaṅgalā3m̐ iti bhāgadugham̐ satyarājā3n iti kṣattāram / tān āhūya brahmaṇe kṣetraṃ dadāti //
13.6.31.a.d: तानपिसृज्य मङ्गल्यनाम्नो ह्वयति सुश्लोका3म्̐ इति संग्रहीतारम्̐ असुमङ्गला3म्̐ इति भागदुघम्̐ सत्यराजा3न् इति क्षत्तारम् । तान् आहूय ब्रह्मणे क्षेत्रं ददाति ॥
13.6.31.a.m: Having discarded them, he calls those who have auspicious names: the charioteer with "O Suśloka!", the collector of taxes with "O Asumaṅgala!", the distributor with "O Satyarājan!"; having called them, he gives land to the brahman priest.

13.6.32.a.m: Whatever the brahman desires, they are the witnesses.

13.6.33.a.s: yāṃ kāmayeta bhāryām asyai prajā rāṣṭram̐ syād iti tasyā aupāsane pratihitam anvārambhayitvā prajāpate na tvad etāni \\ iti ye pātreṣu lopās tair nāmavyatiṣañjanīyau homau juhoti //
13.6.33.a.d: यां कामयेत भार्याम् अस्यै प्रजा राष्ट्रम्̐ स्याद् इति तस्या औपासने प्रतिहितम् अन्वारम्भयित्वा प्रजापते न त्वद् एतानि \\ इति ये पात्रेषु लोपास् तैर् नामव्यतिषञ्जनीयौ होमौ जुहोति ॥
13.6.33.a.m: Whichever wife he should desire, thinking: "May there be offspring, may there be a realm for her," having made the pratihita take hold [of her] from behind at her domestic fire, he offers, with: "O Prajāpati, none other than you [has encompassed all] these [born things]," the two offerings that intertwine names, using the remnants left in the vessels.

13.6.34.a.s: asāv āmuṣyāyaṇo 'muṣyā asau putras \\ iti nāmanī vyatiṣajati //
13.6.34.a.d: असाव् आमुष्यायणो ऽमुष्या असौ पुत्रस् \\ इति नामनी व्यतिषजति ॥
13.6.34.a.m: He intertwines the two names with: "So-and-so, son of so-and-so, is so-and-so's son."

13.6.35.a.s: śaunaḥśepam ākhyāpayate / ṛco gāthāmiśrāḥ // paraḥśatāḥ praḥsahasrā vā //
13.6.35.a.d: शौनःशेपम् आख्यापयते । ऋचो गाथामिश्राः ॥ परःशताः प्रःसहस्रा वा ॥
13.6.35.a.m: He has the legend of Śunaḥśepa recited: ṛc verses mixed with narrative verses, over a hundred, or over a thousand.

13.6.36.a.m: Seated on a golden cushion, the hotṛ recites.

13.6.37.a.s: hiraṇyakūrcayos tiṣṭhann adhvaryuḥ pratigṛṇāti / om ity ṛcaḥ pratigaras tathā \\ iti gāthāyāḥ //
13.6.37.a.d: हिरण्यकूर्चयोस् तिष्ठन्न् अध्वर्युः प्रतिगृणाति । ओम् इत्य् ऋचः प्रतिगरस् तथा \\ इति गाथायाः ॥
13.6.37.a.m: Standing on two golden bundles of grass, the adhvaryu responds. "Om" is the response to an ṛc verse, "So be it" to a narrative verse.

13.6.38.a.s: apavṛtte śaunaḥśepe hiraṇyakaśipuṃ hotre dadāti / hiraṇyakūrcāv adhvaryave //
13.6.38.a.d: अपवृत्ते शौनःशेपे हिरण्यकशिपुं होत्रे ददाति । हिरण्यकूर्चाव् अध्वर्यवे ॥
13.6.38.a.m: When the legend of Śunaḥśepa is completed, he gives the golden cushion to the hotṛ, and the two golden bundles of grass to the adhvaryu.

13.6.39.a.s: atra mārutenaikavim̐śatikapālena vaiśvadevyāmikṣayā pracaret / enā vyāghraṃ pariṣasvajānāḥ \ sim̐ham̐ hinvanti mahate saubhagāya / \ samudraṃ na suhutaṃ tasthivām̐sam \\ marmṛjyante dvīpinam apsv antar ity avadāsyan puroḍāśam abhicaran sphyena samayā vibhindyāt / sphya āśliṣyed yac cāvamārjet tad viṣṇava urukramāyāvadyet /
13.6.39.a.d: अत्र मारुतेनैकविम्̐शतिकपालेन वैश्वदेव्यामिक्षया प्रचरेत् । एना व्याघ्रं परिषस्वजानाः \ सिम्̐हम्̐ हिन्वन्ति महते सौभगाय । \ समुद्रं न सुहुतं तस्थिवाम्̐सम् \\ मर्मृज्यन्ते द्वीपिनम् अप्स्व् अन्तर् इत्य् अवदास्यन् पुरोडाशम् अभिचरन् स्फ्येन समया विभिन्द्यात् । स्फ्य आश्लिष्येद् यच् चावमार्जेत् तद् विष्णव उरुक्रमायावद्येत् ।
13.6.39.a.m: At this point he should proceed with [the cake] on twenty-one potsherds for the Maruts, and with the curds for the Viśvedevas. Intending to cut off the cake, practising sorcery, he should split it right through the middle with the wooden sword, [reciting:] "Embracing the tiger with these, / they impel the lion to great fortune; / like an ocean standing, well-offered, / they cleanse the leopard within the waters." What adheres to the wooden sword and what he wipes off, that he should cut off for Viṣṇu of wide strides.

13.6.40.a.s: atraite hiraṇye dadāti / sauvarṇaṃ rājataṃ maṇiṃ ca / yadi purastād datte bhavataḥ //
13.6.40.a.d: अत्रैते हिरण्ये ददाति । सौवर्णं राजतं मणिं च । यदि पुरस्ताद् दत्ते भवतः ॥
13.6.40.a.m: At this point he gives these two gold pieces—one of gold, one of silver—and a jewel, if they have not been given previously.

13.6.41.a.m: He proceeds to the rites beginning with the Māhendra cup.

13.6.42.a.s: avabhṛthād udetya \\ apāṃ naptre svāhā \\ ity apsu juhoti //
13.6.42.a.d: अवभृथाद् उदेत्य \\ अपां नप्त्रे स्वाहा \\ इत्य् अप्सु जुहोति ॥
13.6.42.a.m: Having come up from the purificatory bath, he offers into the water with: "To the child of the waters, svāhā!"

13.6.43.a.s: ūrjo naptre svāhā \\ iti śuṣke sthāṇau darbhastambe vā //
13.6.43.a.d: ऊर्जो नप्त्रे स्वाहा \\ इति शुष्के स्थाणौ दर्भस्तम्बे वा ॥
13.6.43.a.m: With: "To the child of strength, svāhā!" on a dry stump or a clump of darbha grass.

13.6.44.a.s: agnaye gṛhapataye svāhā \\ iti pratyetya gārhapatye //
13.6.44.a.d: अग्नये गृहपतये स्वाहा \\ इति प्रत्येत्य गार्हपत्ये ॥
13.6.44.a.m: Having returned, with: "To Agni, lord of the house, svāhā!" in the gārhapatya fire.

13.6.45.a.m: He binds as the concluding animal sacrifice a barren cow that has calved, dedicated to Indra.

13.6.46.a.s: tasyā naivāraṃ paśupuroḍāśaṃ catuṣpadyāḥ sūnāyā nirvapati //
13.6.46.a.d: तस्या नैवारं पशुपुरोडाशं चतुष्पद्याः सूनाया निर्वपति ॥
13.6.46.a.m: For its animal cake, he pours out nivāra grain from a four-legged slaughter-bench.

13.6.46.b.m: It takes the place of the cart.

13.7.1.a.s: śvo bhūte saptabhiḥ sam̐sṛpām̐ havirbhir anvahaṃ yajate / āgneyam aṣṭākapālaṃ nirvapatīti yathāsamāmnātam / pūrvaṃpūrvaṃ devayajanam adhyavasyati / yatrāhavanīyaḥ pūrvaḥ syāt tatrāparasyā gārhapatyaḥ saptamyā iṣṭeḥ prāgvam̐śa āhavanīyo bahir gārhapatyaḥ //
13.7.1.a.d: श्वो भूते सप्तभिः सम्̐सृपाम्̐ हविर्भिर् अन्वहं यजते । आग्नेयम् अष्टाकपालं निर्वपतीति यथासमाम्नातम् । पूर्वंपूर्वं देवयजनम् अध्यवस्यति । यत्राहवनीयः पूर्वः स्यात् तत्रापरस्या गार्हपत्यः सप्तम्या इष्टेः प्राग्वम्̐श आहवनीयो बहिर् गार्हपत्यः ॥
13.7.1.a.m: On the next day, he sacrifices day after day with the seven Saṃsṛp oblations. He pours out [an oblation] on eight potsherds for Agni, as handed down by tradition. Each time, he establishes a sacrificial site further ahead: where the earlier āhavanīya fire was, there is the gārhapatya fire of the next. For the seventh offering, the āhavanīya is in the eastern hall, the gārhapatya is outside.

13.7.2.a.s: atha tayā yajate / tasyām̐ sam̐sthitāyām aparāhṇe daśapeyāya dīkṣate //
13.7.2.a.d: अथ तया यजते । तस्याम्̐ सम्̐स्थितायाम् अपराह्णे दशपेयाय दीक्षते ॥
13.7.2.a.m: Then he sacrifices with it. When it has concluded, in the afternoon he is consecrated for the Daśapeya.

13.7.3.a.s: apsu dīkṣāyāḥ sthāne ṣaṭpuṇḍarīkāṃ dvādaśapuṇḍarīkāṃ vā hiraṇyasrajaṃ yajamānaḥ pratimuñcate //
13.7.3.a.d: अप्सु दीक्षायाः स्थाने षट्पुण्डरीकां द्वादशपुण्डरीकां वा हिरण्यस्रजं यजमानः प्रतिमुञ्चते ॥
13.7.3.a.m: Instead of the consecration in the waters, the sacrificer puts on a golden garland of six lotuses or twelve lotuses.

13.7.4.a.s: tad ahar dīkṣito rājānaṃ krīṇāti daśabhir vatsataraiḥ sāṇḍaiḥ //
13.7.4.a.d: तद् अहर् दीक्षितो राजानं क्रीणाति दशभिर् वत्सतरैः साण्डैः ॥
13.7.4.a.m: On that day, having been consecrated, he buys the king [soma] with ten one-year-old uncastrated bulls.

13.7.5.a.m: He does not bargain; he does not carry it around.

13.7.6.a.m: He merely carries out a second purchase.

13.7.7.a.s: purastād upasadām̐ saumyaṃ caruṃ nirvapati / antarā tvāṣṭram upariṣṭād vaiṣṇavam //
13.7.7.a.d: पुरस्ताद् उपसदाम्̐ सौम्यं चरुं निर्वपति । अन्तरा त्वाष्ट्रम् उपरिष्टाद् वैष्णवम् ॥
13.7.7.a.m: Before the Upasad days, he pours out a caru for Soma; in between, one for Tvaṣṭṛ; after, one for Viṣṇu.

13.7.8.a.s: tāsām aupasadaṃ bahiḥ paridhayaś cārtham̐ sādhayanti //
13.7.8.a.d: तासाम् औपसदं बहिः परिधयश् चार्थम्̐ साधयन्ति ॥
13.7.8.a.m: The grass and enclosing sticks of the Upasad rites accomplish their purpose.

13.7.9.a.m: The Daśapeya is a seventeen-versed Agniṣṭoma. The vasatīvarī waters are taken from the Sarasvatī.

13.7.10.a.s: bhārgavo hotā bhavati / śrāyantīyaṃ brahmasāmaṃ bhavati / vāravantīyam agniṣṭomasāmam //
13.7.10.a.d: भार्गवो होता भवति । श्रायन्तीयं ब्रह्मसामं भवति । वारवन्तीयम् अग्निष्टोमसामम् ॥
13.7.10.a.m: The hotṛ is a Bhārgava; the Śrāyantīya is the saman of the brahman; the Vāravantīya is the Agniṣṭomasāman.

13.7.11.a.m: At the time of arranging the vessels, he sets down ten additional cups.

13.7.12.a.m: At the time of drawing [the soma], he draws ten additional cups.

13.7.13.a.s: bhakṣaṇakāle ya ā daśamāt puruṣād avicchinnasomapīthaḥ sa bhakṣasya kartā daśamāt puruṣād anvākhyāya śataṃ brāhmaṇāḥ somapāḥ saṃprasarpanti //
13.7.13.a.d: भक्षणकाले य आ दशमात् पुरुषाद् अविच्छिन्नसोमपीथः स भक्षस्य कर्ता दशमात् पुरुषाद् अन्वाख्याय शतं ब्राह्मणाः सोमपाः संप्रसर्पन्ति ॥
13.7.13.a.m: At the time of consuming: he whose soma-drinking is unbroken up to the tenth generation is one entitled to consume; having recounted up to the tenth generation, one hundred soma-drinking brāhmaṇas glide forward.

13.7.14.a.m: Ten by ten, they consume each cup.

13.7.15.a.s: dakṣiṇākāle hiraṇyaprākāśāv adhvaryave dadātīti yathāsamāmnātam / ukṣāṇaṃ grāvastute vehāyamānām ivonnetre bastam̐ subrahmaṇyāya //
13.7.15.a.d: दक्षिणाकाले हिरण्यप्राकाशाव् अध्वर्यवे ददातीति यथासमाम्नातम् । उक्षाणं ग्रावस्तुते वेहायमानाम् इवोन्नेत्रे बस्तम्̐ सुब्रह्मण्याय ॥
13.7.15.a.m: At the time of the sacrificial gifts, he gives two gold mirrors to the adhvaryu, as handed down by tradition; an ox to the grāvastut; a seemingly barren cow to the unnetṛ; a he-goat to the subrahmaṇya.

13.7.17.a.m: When it has concluded, he sacrifices with the Aveṣṭi of the quarters.

13.7.18.a.s: āgneyam aṣṭākapālaṃ nirvapatīti yathāsamāmnātam̐ haviṣohaviṣa iṣṭvā bārhaspatyaṃ pratyabhighārayet //
13.7.18.a.d: आग्नेयम् अष्टाकपालं निर्वपतीति यथासमाम्नातम्̐ हविषोहविष इष्ट्वा बार्हस्पत्यं प्रत्यभिघारयेत् ॥
13.7.18.a.m: He pours out [an oblation] on eight potsherds for Agni, as handed down by tradition. After sacrificing each oblation, he should baste the [caru] dedicated to Bṛhaspati.

13.7.19.a.m: One who desires proper food or desires heaven should sacrifice with it.

13.7.20.a.s: brāhmaṇo yajamāno madhye vidhāyāhutimāhutim̐ hutvābhighārayeta / yadi rājanya aindram / yadi vaiśyo vaiśvadevam //
13.7.20.a.d: ब्राह्मणो यजमानो मध्ये विधायाहुतिमाहुतिम्̐ हुत्वाभिघारयेत । यदि राजन्य ऐन्द्रम् । यदि वैश्यो वैश्वदेवम् ॥
13.7.20.a.m: If the sacrificer is a brāhmaṇa, having placed it in the middle and having offered each oblation, he should baste [the Bṛhaspati caru]; if he is a rājanya, [the oblation] for Indra; if he is a vaiśya, [the oblation] for the Viśvedevas.

13.7.21.a.m: On the next day, he should sacrifice with an animal sacrifice of two victims.

13.7.22.a.s: ādityāṃ malhāṃ garbhiṇīm ālabhate / mārutīṃ pṛśniṃ paṣṭhahīm / aśvibhyām aupām̐śu mārutyā pracarati / āśrutapratyāśrute apy upām̐śu bhavataḥ / uccair ādityāyāḥ //
13.7.22.a.d: आदित्यां मल्हां गर्भिणीम् आलभते । मारुतीं पृश्निं पष्ठहीम् । अश्विभ्याम् औपाम्̐शु मारुत्या प्रचरति । आश्रुतप्रत्याश्रुते अप्य् उपाम्̐शु भवतः । उच्चैर् आदित्यायाः ॥
13.7.22.a.m: He binds a dewlapped, pregnant [heifer] for Aditi, and a dappled, four-year-old heifer for the Maruts. He proceeds inaudibly for the Aśvins with the one for the Maruts; the calls and responses are also inaudible; aloud for the one dedicated to Aditi.

13.7.23.a.s: tataḥ śvo bhūte ṣaḍbhiḥ prayujām̐ havirbhir yajate //
13.7.23.a.d: ततः श्वो भूते षड्भिः प्रयुजाम्̐ हविर्भिर् यजते ॥
13.7.23.a.m: Then, on the next day, he sacrifices with the six Prayuj oblations.

13.7.24.a.s: āgneyam aṣṭākapālaṃ nirvapatīti yathāsamāmnātam / dakṣiṇo rathavāhanavāho dakṣiṇā //
13.7.24.a.d: आग्नेयम् अष्टाकपालं निर्वपतीति यथासमाम्नातम् । दक्षिणो रथवाहनवाहो दक्षिणा ॥
13.7.24.a.m: He pours out [an oblation] on eight potsherds for Agni, as handed down by tradition. The right-hand chariot draft-horse is the sacrificial gift.

13.7.25.a.s: śvo bhūte ṣaḍbhir uttaraiḥ sārasvataṃ caruṃ nirvapatīti yathāsamāmnātam // tisṛdhanvam̐ śuṣkadṛtir daṇḍam upānahau ca taddakṣiṇāśvo vā / śoṇakarṇa ity ekeṣām / tat pratirājabhyaḥ prahiṇoti //
13.7.25.a.d: श्वो भूते षड्भिर् उत्तरैः सारस्वतं चरुं निर्वपतीति यथासमाम्नातम् ॥ तिसृधन्वम्̐ शुष्कदृतिर् दण्डम् उपानहौ च तद्दक्षिणाश्वो वा । शोणकर्ण इत्य् एकेषाम् । तत् प्रतिराजभ्यः प्रहिणोति ॥
13.7.25.a.m: On the next day, with the following six [oblations], he pours out a caru for Sarasvatī, as handed down by tradition. A three-arrow bow, a dry waterskin, a staff, and two sandals are its sacrificial gift, or a horse; according to some, a horse with red ears. He dispatches that to the rival kings.

13.7.26.a.m: He announces: "I have been consecrated; I have become king."

13.7.27.a.m: For a year he offers the Agnihotra.

13.7.28.a.s: anusaṃtatyai tatra ye 'gnihotreṇāpratiṣiddhāḥ kratavas tān āharet //
13.7.28.a.d: अनुसंतत्यै तत्र ये ऽग्निहोत्रेणाप्रतिषिद्धाः क्रतवस् तान् आहरेत् ॥
13.7.28.a.m: For continuity, he should undertake during that [period] those sacrifices that are not barred by the Agnihotra.

13.7.29.a.m: At the end of the year, he sacrifices with the Keśavapanīya Atirātra.

13.7.30.a.s: tatra vapanapravādā mantrās teṣām ādipravādair ādito vāpayetāntapravādair antataḥ / saṃtiṣṭhate keśavapanīyaḥ //
13.7.30.a.d: तत्र वपनप्रवादा मन्त्रास् तेषाम् आदिप्रवादैर् आदितो वापयेतान्तप्रवादैर् अन्ततः । संतिष्ठते केशवपनीयः ॥
13.7.30.a.m: There the mantras mention shaving: with those mentioning the beginning, he should have [the hair] shaved from the beginning; with those mentioning the end, towards the end. The Keśavapanīya is concluded.

13.7.31.a.m: When it has concluded, he should sacrifice with the Vyuṣṭidvirātra.

13.7.32.a.d: तस्य ज्योतिष्टोमो ऽग्निष्टोमः पूर्वम् अहर् भवति ॥
13.7.32.a.m: Its first day is a Jyotiṣṭoma Agniṣṭoma.

13.7.33.a.s: sarvastomo 'tirātra uttaraṃ gāyatraṃ pūrve 'hant sāma bhavati / traiṣṭubham uttaram / rathaṃtaraṃ pūrve 'hant sāma bhavati / bṛhad uttare vaikhānasam / pūrve 'hant sāma bhavati / ṣoḍaśy uttare haviṣman nidhanaṃ pūrvam ahar bhavati / haviṣkṛn nidhanam uttaram / amāvāsyāyāṃ pūrvam ahar yajanīyam uttaram / āpūryamāṇapakṣasya vā / ye puṣye ahanī syātām //
13.7.33.a.d: सर्वस्तोमो ऽतिरात्र उत्तरं गायत्रं पूर्वे ऽहन्त् साम भवति । त्रैष्टुभम् उत्तरम् । रथंतरं पूर्वे ऽहन्त् साम भवति । बृहद् उत्तरे वैखानसम् । पूर्वे ऽहन्त् साम भवति । षोडश्य् उत्तरे हविष्मन् निधनं पूर्वम् अहर् भवति । हविष्कृन् निधनम् उत्तरम् । अमावास्यायां पूर्वम् अहर् यजनीयम् उत्तरम् । आपूर्यमाणपक्षस्य वा । ये पुष्ये अहनी स्याताम् ॥
13.7.33.a.m: The second day is an atirātra consisting of all the stomas. On the first day, the chant is in the gāyatrī metre; on the second, in the triṣṭubh metre. On the first day, the chant is the Rathaṃtara; on the second, the Bṛhat. On the first day, the chant is the Vaikhānasa; on the second, the Ṣoḍaśin. The first day has 'haviṣmat' as its cadence; the second day has 'haviṣkṛt' as its cadence. On the new-moon day, the first day is sacrificed, [then] the second; or else on whichever two days of the waxing fortnight are in conjunction with Puṣya.

13.7.34.a.m: The 'Supporter of Rulers' is an agniṣṭoma; he should sacrifice with it at the end.

13.7.37.a.m: Having sacrificed with the Rājasūya, he should sacrifice with the Sautrāmaṇī.

13.8.1.a.s: trirātre purastāt sīsena klībāc chaṣpāṇi krītvā kṣaume vāsasy upanahya nidadhāti //
13.8.1.a.d: त्रिरात्रे पुरस्तात् सीसेन क्लीबाच् छष्पाणि क्रीत्वा क्षौमे वासस्य् उपनह्य निदधाति ॥
13.8.1.a.m: Three nights before, having purchased sprouted barley grains with lead from a eunuch, he ties them up in a linen cloth and deposits them.

13.8.2.a.m: He sets in motion the sacrificial framework of the Sautrāmaṇī.

13.8.3.a.s: tatra yāvat kriyate tad vyākhyāsyāmo 'gnīn anvādhāya vedaṃ kṛtvāgnīn paristīrya pāṇī prakṣālyolaparājīm̐ stīrtvā yathārthaṃ pātrāṇi prayunakti sthālīṃ kapālānām̐ sthāne prayunakti //
13.8.3.a.d: तत्र यावत् क्रियते तद् व्याख्यास्यामो ऽग्नीन् अन्वाधाय वेदं कृत्वाग्नीन् परिस्तीर्य पाणी प्रक्षाल्योलपराजीम्̐ स्तीर्त्वा यथार्थं पात्राणि प्रयुनक्ति स्थालीं कपालानाम्̐ स्थाने प्रयुनक्ति ॥
13.8.3.a.m: In regard to that, we shall explain as much as is performed: having fueled the fires, fashioned the grass broom, strewn grass around the fires, washed his hands, and strewn stalks of reed-grass, he sets out the implements as required; he sets out a pot in place of the potsherds.

13.8.4.a.s: nirvapaṇakāle 'śvibhyām̐ sarasvatyā indrāya sutrāmṇe prabhūtān brīhīn nirvapati //
13.8.4.a.d: निर्वपणकाले ऽश्विभ्याम्̐ सरस्वत्या इन्द्राय सुत्राम्णे प्रभूतान् ब्रीहीन् निर्वपति ॥
13.8.4.a.m: At the time of the apportioning, he portions out an abundance of paddy for the Aśvins, for Sarasvatī, and for Indra the Good Protector.

13.8.5.a.s: carukalpena śrapayitvāgreṇa gārhapatyam avaṭaṃ khātvā surāyāḥ kalpena parisrutam̐ saṃdadhāti //
13.8.5.a.d: चरुकल्पेन श्रपयित्वाग्रेण गार्हपत्यम् अवटं खात्वा सुरायाः कल्पेन परिस्रुतम्̐ संदधाति ॥
13.8.5.a.m: Having cooked [them] in the manner of a caru and dug a hole in front of the gārhapatya fire, he puts together the fermenting liquor in the manner of surā liquor.

13.8.6.a.s: svādvīṃ tvā svādunā \\ iti śaṣpaiḥ surām̐ sam̐sṛjati //
13.8.6.a.d: स्वाद्वीं त्वा स्वादुना \\ इति शष्पैः सुराम्̐ सम्̐सृजति ॥
13.8.6.a.m: With the mantra, 'Thee, sweet, with sweet...', he mixes the surā with the sprouted grains.

13.8.7.a.s: somo 'si \\ aśvibhyāṃ pacyasva \ sarasvatyai pacyasva \\ indrāya sutrāmṇe pacyasva \\ iti sam̐sṛṣṭām abhimantrayate //
13.8.7.a.d: सोमो ऽसि \\ अश्विभ्यां पच्यस्व \ सरस्वत्यै पच्यस्व \\ इन्द्राय सुत्राम्णे पच्यस्व \\ इति सम्̐सृष्टाम् अभिमन्त्रयते ॥
13.8.7.a.m: With the mantra, 'Thou art Soma; ripen for the Aśvins; ripen for Sarasvatī; ripen for Indra the Good Protector', he addresses the mixture with mantras.

13.8.8.a.m: It remains combined for three nights.

13.8.10.a.s: na vedaṃ karoti / purastāt kṛte nārthān kurute //
13.8.10.a.d: न वेदं करोति । पुरस्तात् कृते नार्थान् कुरुते ॥
13.8.10.a.m: He does not make a grass broom; he accomplishes the needs with the one made previously.

13.8.11.a.m: He makes an altar measuring one third of the soma altar.

13.8.12.a.s: yasmin kāle 'dhvaryur uttaravediṃ karoti tasmin kāle pratiprasthātā cātvālāt purīṣam āhṛtya dakṣiṇenottaravediṃ caturaśraṃ kharaṃ karoti //
13.8.12.a.d: यस्मिन् काले ऽध्वर्युर् उत्तरवेदिं करोति तस्मिन् काले प्रतिप्रस्थाता चात्वालात् पुरीषम् आहृत्य दक्षिणेनोत्तरवेदिं चतुरश्रं खरं करोति ॥
13.8.12.a.m: At the time the adhvaryu makes the high altar, at that time the pratiprasthātā, having brought earth from the pits, makes a square mound to the south of the high altar.

13.8.13.a.s: yasmin kāle 'dhvaryur āhavanīyaṃ praṇayati tasmin kāle pratiprasthātā dakṣiṇāgner aṅgārān āhṛtya khare nyupyopasamādadhāti //
13.8.13.a.d: यस्मिन् काले ऽध्वर्युर् आहवनीयं प्रणयति तस्मिन् काले प्रतिप्रस्थाता दक्षिणाग्नेर् अङ्गारान् आहृत्य खरे न्युप्योपसमादधाति ॥
13.8.13.a.m: At the time the adhvaryu leads forward the āhavanīya fire, at that time the pratiprasthātā, having brought embers from the dakṣiṇāgni fire, pours them out upon the mound and maintains the fire upon it.

13.8.15.a.s: aśvibhyām̐ sarasvatyā indrāya sutrāmṇe trīṇi vaikaṅkatāny ūrdhvapātrāṇi prayunakti //
13.8.15.a.d: अश्विभ्याम्̐ सरस्वत्या इन्द्राय सुत्राम्णे त्रीणि वैकङ्कतान्य् ऊर्ध्वपात्राणि प्रयुनक्ति ॥
13.8.15.a.m: He sets out three tall vessels of Vikankata wood for the Aśvins, for Sarasvatī, and for Indra the Good Protector.

13.8.16.a.s: satam̐ śatātṛṇṇām̐ sthālīṃ rukmaṃ vālasrāvaṃ ca //
13.8.16.a.d: सतम्̐ शतातृण्णाम्̐ स्थालीं रुक्मं वालस्रावं च ॥
13.8.16.a.m: He also sets out a wide-mouthed dish, a pot pierced with a hundred holes, a gold plate, and a horsehair sieve.

13.8.17.a.s: yat prāk paśūpākaraṇāt kṛtvodbhidya surām̐ sate niṣicya punātu te parisrutam iti vālamayena pavitreṇa punāti //
13.8.17.a.d: यत् प्राक् पशूपाकरणात् कृत्वोद्भिद्य सुराम्̐ सते निषिच्य पुनातु ते परिस्रुतम् इति वालमयेन पवित्रेण पुनाति ॥
13.8.17.a.m: Having performed whatever rites precede the bringing up of the victim, having uncovered the surā and poured it into the wide-mouthed dish, he strains it through the horsehair strainer with the mantra, 'May thy fermenting liquor purify...';

13.8.18.a.s: vāyuḥ pūtaḥ pavitreṇa \\ iti somavāminaḥ / somātipavitasya vā / prāṅ somas \\ iti somātipavitasya pūtāṃ brāhmaṇasya mūrdhan sādayitvā //
13.8.18.a.d: वायुः पूतः पवित्रेण \\ इति सोमवामिनः । सोमातिपवितस्य वा । प्राङ् सोमस् \\ इति सोमातिपवितस्य पूतां ब्राह्मणस्य मूर्धन् सादयित्वा ॥
13.8.18.a.m: with 'Vāyu is purified by the strainer...' for one who has vomited soma or one over-purified by soma; or with 'Forward soma...' for one over-purified by soma; and having placed the purified [surā] upon the head of a Brahmin,

13.8.19.a.s: paśūpākaraṇaprabhṛtīni karmāṇi pratipadyate / āśvinam ajaṃ dhūmram upākaroti / sārasvataṃ ca meṣam aindram ṛṣabhaṃ vṛṣṇiṃ bastaṃ vā / bārhaspatyaṃ caturtham̐ somavāminaḥ somātipavitasya vā //
13.8.19.a.d: पशूपाकरणप्रभृतीनि कर्माणि प्रतिपद्यते । आश्विनम् अजं धूम्रम् उपाकरोति । सारस्वतं च मेषम् ऐन्द्रम् ऋषभं वृष्णिं बस्तं वा । बार्हस्पत्यं चतुर्थम्̐ सोमवामिनः सोमातिपवितस्य वा ॥
13.8.19.a.m: he undertakes the rites beginning with the bringing up of the victim. He brings up a smoky-grey goat for the Aśvins, a ram for Sarasvatī, a bull, ram, or he-goat for Indra; and a fourth for Bṛhaspati in the case of one who has vomited soma or one over-purified by soma.

13.8.20.a.s: hutāsu vapāsu rukmam ṛṣabham̐ sātvarīṃ ca vaḍavāṃ dakṣiṇām dadāti //
13.8.20.a.d: हुतासु वपासु रुक्मम् ऋषभम्̐ सात्वरीं च वडवां दक्षिणाम् ददाति ॥
13.8.20.a.m: When the omenta are offered, he gives as sacrificial gift a gold plate, a bull, and an ambling mare.

13.8.21.a.s: tat kṛtvā vāyavyaiḥ surāgrahān gṛhṇānti \\ upayāmagṛhīto 'si \\ acchidrāṃ tvācchidreṇāśvibhyāṃ juṣṭaṃ gṛhṇāmi \\ ity āśvinaṃ graham adhvaryur gṛhṇāti / upayāmagṛhīto 'si \\ acchidrāṃ tvācchidreṇa sarasvatyai juṣṭaṃ gṛhṇāmi \\ iti sārasvatam / pratiprasthātā / upayāmagṛhīto 'si \\ acchidrāṃ svāc chidreṇendrāya sutrāmṇe juṣṭaṃ gṛhṇāmi \\ ity aindraṃ yajamānaḥ //
13.8.21.a.d: तत् कृत्वा वायव्यैः सुराग्रहान् गृह्णान्ति \\ उपयामगृहीतो ऽसि \\ अच्छिद्रां त्वाच्छिद्रेणाश्विभ्यां जुष्टं गृह्णामि \\ इत्य् आश्विनं ग्रहम् अध्वर्युर् गृह्णाति । उपयामगृहीतो ऽसि \\ अच्छिद्रां त्वाच्छिद्रेण सरस्वत्यै जुष्टं गृह्णामि \\ इति सारस्वतम् । प्रतिप्रस्थाता । उपयामगृहीतो ऽसि \\ अच्छिद्रां स्वाच् छिद्रेणेन्द्राय सुत्राम्णे जुष्टं गृह्णामि \\ इत्य् ऐन्द्रं यजमानः ॥
13.8.21.a.m: Having done that, they draw the surā cups with vāyavya cups. With the mantra, 'Thou art taken with a base; thee free from flaws with flawlessness, I draw agreeable to the Aśvins', the adhvaryu draws the Aśvina cup. With 'Thou art taken with a base; thee free from flaws with flawlessness, I draw agreeable to Sarasvatī', the pratiprasthātā [draws] the Sārasvata cup. With 'Thou art taken with a base; thee free from flaws with flawlessness, I draw agreeable to Indra the Good Protector', the sacrificer [draws] the Aindra cup.

13.8.22.a.s: kuvid aṅga \\ iti sarveṣām ekā puroruk //
13.8.22.a.d: कुविद् अङ्ग \\ इति सर्वेषाम् एका पुरोरुक् ॥
13.8.22.a.m: 'Where indeed, pray...' is the single preparatory verse for all of them.

13.8.23.a.s: kvalasaktubhir āśvinam̐ śrīṇāti / badarasaktubhir ity ekeṣām / sim̐halomabhiś ca karkandhūsaktubhiḥ sārasvatam̐ śārdūlalomabhiś ca badarasaktubhir aindraṃ kvakalasaktubhir ity ekeṣām / vṛkalomabhiś ca / api vā sim̐hā vadhvaryur manasā dhyāyet / śārdūlaiḥ pratiprasthātā / vṛkair yajamānaḥ //
13.8.23.a.d: क्वलसक्तुभिर् आश्विनम्̐ श्रीणाति । बदरसक्तुभिर् इत्य् एकेषाम् । सिम्̐हलोमभिश् च कर्कन्धूसक्तुभिः सारस्वतम्̐ शार्दूललोमभिश् च बदरसक्तुभिर् ऐन्द्रं क्वकलसक्तुभिर् इत्य् एकेषाम् । वृकलोमभिश् च । अपि वा सिम्̐हा वध्वर्युर् मनसा ध्यायेत् । शार्दूलैः प्रतिप्रस्थाता । वृकैर् यजमानः ॥
13.8.23.a.m: He mixes the Aśvina [cup] with flour of jujube berries—with flour of common jujubes according to some—and hairs of a lion; the Sārasvata [cup] with flour of wild jujubes and hairs of a tiger; the Aindra [cup] with flour of common jujubes—with flour of jujube berries according to some—and hairs of a wolf. Or rather, the adhvaryu should meditate mentally on lions, the pratiprasthātā on tigers, and the sacrificer on wolves.

13.8.24.a.s: eṣa te yonis \\ aśvibhyāṃ tvā \ eṣa te yoniḥ \ sarasvatyai tvā \ eṣa te yonis \\ indrāya tvā sutrāmṇe \\ iti yathārūpaṃ brāhmaṇasya mūrdhan sādayayitvā //
13.8.24.a.d: एष ते योनिस् \\ अश्विभ्यां त्वा \ एष ते योनिः \ सरस्वत्यै त्वा \ एष ते योनिस् \\ इन्द्राय त्वा सुत्राम्णे \\ इति यथारूपं ब्राह्मणस्य मूर्धन् सादययित्वा ॥
13.8.24.a.m: With the mantras, 'This is thy womb; thee for the Aśvins; this is thy womb; thee for Sarasvatī; this is thy womb; thee for Indra the Good Protector', having deposited [the cups] respectively upon the head of the Brahmin,

13.8.25.a.s: paśupuroḍāśaprabhṛtīni karmāṇi pratipadyate // bārhaspatyaṃ paśupuroḍāśaṃ nirupyaindram ekādaśakapālaṃ nirvapati / sāvitraṃ dvādaśakapālam / vāruṇaṃ daśakapālam //
13.8.25.a.d: पशुपुरोडाशप्रभृतीनि कर्माणि प्रतिपद्यते ॥ बार्हस्पत्यं पशुपुरोडाशं निरुप्यैन्द्रम् एकादशकपालं निर्वपति । सावित्रं द्वादशकपालम् । वारुणं दशकपालम् ॥
13.8.25.a.m: he undertakes the rites beginning with the cake offering for the victim. Having portioned out the animal-cake for Bṛhaspati, he portions out an eleven-potsherd cake for Indra, a twelve-potsherd cake for Savitṛ, and a ten-potsherd cake for Varuṇa.

13.8.26.a.s: tān āsādya yathāgṛhītaṃ grahān ādadate \\ aśvibhyām̐ sarasvatyā indrāya sutrāmṇe somānām̐ surāṇām anubrūhi / \ aśvibhyām̐ sarasvatyā indrāya sutrāmṇe somān surān prasthitān preṣya \\ iti saṃpreṣyati //
13.8.26.a.d: तान् आसाद्य यथागृहीतं ग्रहान् आददते \\ अश्विभ्याम्̐ सरस्वत्या इन्द्राय सुत्राम्णे सोमानाम्̐ सुराणाम् अनुब्रूहि । \ अश्विभ्याम्̐ सरस्वत्या इन्द्राय सुत्राम्णे सोमान् सुरान् प्रस्थितान् प्रेष्य \\ इति संप्रेष्यति ॥
13.8.26.a.m: Having placed them, they take up the cups as drawn, and he gives the ritual direction: 'Recite the introductory verse for the somas and surās for the Aśvins, for Sarasvatī, and for Indra the Good Protector; prompt [the hotṛ] for the somas and surās set forth for the Aśvins, for Sarasvatī, and for Indra the Good Protector.'
